Sports.title: Kyle Walker lined up for shock Premier League return
Sports.content:
Everton are considering a move for Kyle Walker.

The Burnley right-back has 12 months remaining on his deal at Turf Moor having joined the club from Manchester City last summer.

3 Walker (right) could do little to prevent Burnley from slipping into the Championship last season Credit: Getty



Walker, who has come close to joining Everton on multiple occasions during his career, could finally land at Hill Dickinson Stadium this summer.

The 36-year-old has continued to show his reliability having started 35 times in the Premier League for the Clarets in last season’s relegation campaign.

And he showed that he can still be decisive by netting Burnley’s winning penalty in Saturday’s Carabao Cup win over Notts County.

The move would provide Walker with another welcome shot at Premier League football despite his summer preparation for Championship football.



The Sun reports that Everton boss David Moyes is keen to bring in Walker, who boasts a wealth of experience ahead of a busy campaign for the Toffees with European qualification among the club’s objectives.

The right-back position is an area of concern for Moyes who has deployed centre-back Jake O’Brien as a make-shift full-back.



Everton are facing up to life without Seamus Coleman who left the club last summer while Nathan Patterson has failed to cement himself as a credible long-term successor to the Irishman.

Moyes will be hoping to fill the gap in time for their clash against Crystal Palace on the opening weekend of the season.



Moyes' shopping spree

The Everton boss has already been active in this summer’s transfer window with the additions of Christian Norgaard, Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Merlin Rohl.

Everton tied up to the signing of Brennan Johnson from Crystal Palace on Tuesday as part of a swap deal that saw Dwight McNeil move in the opposite direction.

3 Walker was almost an ever present in the Premier League for Burnley last season, clocking up 35 games Credit: Getty

After completing his switch to the Merseyside club, Johnson said: “I’m so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it’s a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.



“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in.

“You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

“I want to come in and show what I can do. The manager spoke to me about getting back to the form that I’ve shown previously, and that’s a massive thing for me – the fact he knows and believes in what I can do...

“For me, listening to him – a manager who is so experienced and someone who has been so successful – it was really nice to hear.



“I want to bring all of my attributes. First and foremost, I’ll work for the team, the fans, and represent the Club properly.

3 Everton can call upon Brennan Johnson after the Wales international sealed his switch from Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

“I know that’s something that’s definitely appreciated and a non-negotiable here. They can expect that from me. On top of that, I think I can bring speed, goals and everything I’ve got.

“The incredible fanbase that Everton has, whether it’s home or away, is something I’ve always felt. It’s a massive honour to be here and play for them now.”

Sports.title: Abbi Summers: I’ve never disliked a captain more but this is why Cristian Romero to Arsenal can’t happen
Sports.content:
Abbi Summers: I’ve never disliked a captain more but this is why Cristian Romero to Arsenal can’t happen

Cristian Romero can dream of a move to Arsenal but in reality, it’s a transfer that will never be sanctioned.

That’s the view of talkSPORT’s Abbi Summers who has never hidden her disapproval of the Spurs captain.



5 Tottenham fans have had enough of Romero and Abbi Summers wants him gone - just not to Arsenal Credit: Getty

Summers has issued multiple passionate rants pertaining to the Argentine’s succession of controversial incidents both on and off the pitch.

talkSPORT understands Romero is set to join Atletico Madrid despite Tottenham initially agreeing a £34million deal with Napoli.

Meanwhile, Inter Milan held talks with the defender earlier this summer.



However, shock reports could point to an almighty twist in the future of Romero with recent suggestions that bitter rivals Arsenal could be ready to swoop for Romero has sparked Summers into yet another rant on the Spurs skipper.

The Gunners are reportedly open to bolstering their back line with William Saliba set for an extended spell on the sidelines due to a back injury.



The idea of Romero, who is under contract until 2029, moving to Arsenal instantly brings back memories of Sol Campbell’s infamous move across the north London divide in 2001 which still haunts Tottenham fans 25 years later.

Does Summers believe Romero would entertain a move to Arsenal?

“I don’t know him personally, he could be the nicest bloke in the world but I can only judge him as a footballer and the type of character I see on the pitch,” Summers said of Romero on her new talkSPORT YouTube channel.



“And yeah, I could see that actually being something he’d be open to. Why wouldn’t you want to go to the champions, let’s be honest?”

“He clearly doesn’t have any love, care or respect for Spurs in my opinion. I don't feel like I've ever seen that from him.

“It’s always been Argentina first, Spurs second.”

5 Summers says Romero lacks respect for Spurs whilst pouring all his passion into playing for his country, which wound up England supporters during the World Cup Credit: Getty

Despite that, Summers is not convinced that a move to Arsenal would ever be a realistic opportunity for the Argentine.



“I cannot see a world where Tottenham would ever sanction a move,” she added.

“We’re not just talking about a young player here. We’re talking about a senior player who is the club captain crossing the divide, going to Arsenal.

“I cannot see a world where Tottenham, the hierarchy – even though I don’t think much of them – I just don’t think that they would allow that to happen.

“Let’s be honest, if that actually occurred and he went and played for Arsenal, imagine what that would be like in a north London derby.



“I don’t even know if he’d be able to enter Tottenham High Road. I don’t even know if he’d be able to enter the stadium.

5 Sol Campbell was vilified by Tottenham fans when he joined Arsenal for free in 2001 and they have not forgotten the betrayal Credit: Getty

“I think where we’re so deeply traumatised and scarred by the Sol Campbell stuff, you can’t let your captain or any player go to Arsenal.

“I wouldn’t care if he went to Man United, Man City or somewhere else but we’re talking about a club like Arsenal.



“It’s the same with Chelsea. Spurs don’t do business with Chelsea, we don’t do business with Arsenal and we're certainly not going to allow the club captain, even if that’s what he wants, to make that move.”

No fee would be enough to sell Romero to Arsenal

Summers even claimed that a nine-figure sum would not be enough to tempt Spurs into strengthening their rivals ahead of next season’s title defence.

“It doesn’t matter if Arsenal offered me £100million. You cannot in principle let the captain of your football club go to your biggest rivals.

“I don’t really care what he goes for, I just want him away from the club but I do care that the location is not Arsenal.



5 Abbi is no fan of Romero, but definitely doesn't want him turning out in red and celebrating in a north London derby on the other side

“I think he would be a perfect fit for someone like Cheslea. I think Romero as a player is so Chelsea coded but I still wouldn’t want him to go to Chelsea.

“If it was other Premier League side’s out of those two I wouldn’t really care.”

And while Summers admitted that Romero does pose world-class attributes at times, she concluded with a message for La Liga’s two interested parties.



“I can understand why any club would want him even with the disciplinary record and the headloss,” she said

“It can be beaten out of someone in a way and I think playing in a different team with different standards which I do believe are set not only by the manager but also the captain.

“They set the standards. He was the one setting the standards. He was also late to training.

5 Roberto De Zerbi is already planning for life after Romero Credit: Getty



“Look at the mentality of what has gone on at my football club over the last couple of years compared to other football clubs.

“When the standards and the bar is so low, that is felt around everywhere and it’s not a surprise that Spurs were in a relegation battle and finished 17th two seasons in a row.

“If Atletico or Barca want a player that is extremely hotheaded, temperamental, unpredictable. Please be my guest.

“I’ve never disliked a club captain I don't think and I’m actually really excited for the new season because I feel it's a fresh start.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo confirms he and Georgina Rodriguez are married in candid post
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo confirms he and Georgina Rodriguez are married in candid post

Cristiano Ronaldo has officially tied the knot with long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez.

The Portuguese superstar got married to model Rodríguez in a civil ceremony on Tuesday.



4 Ronaldo and Rodriguez wed in a private ceremony Credit: Instagram

The ceremony took place in Cascais, Portugal a year to the day since the pair, who share two children together, announced their engagement on Instagram in 2025.

"Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife," a representative for the Al Nassr star said.

"The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children."



Ronaldo took to Instagram once again to announce that the two had officially wed, posting a picture of the couple holding hands with their wedding bands with the caption: "C❤️G."

The wedding took place just days after it was believed that they would be tying the knot in Funchal Cathedral - Ronaldo's hometown - leading to thousands of fans gathering outside of the church.



How did Ronaldo and Rodríguez meet?

The two met back in 2016 when Argentine-Spanish Rodríguez was working at a Gucci store in Madrid.

In her Netflix documentary entitled 'Soy Georgina' (I am Georgina), the 42-year-old revealed that their meeting came by chance as she was supposed to leave work earlier that day, only to be asked to assist a special VIP client - Ronaldo, then playing for La Liga giants Real Madrid.



"I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends," she shared in the documentary," she said.

"Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach."

After that meeting, the two have been virtually inseparable, with Ronaldo often picking her up from work in his Bugatti after she had arrived via bus.

4 The two announced they had wed on Tuesday Credit: Instagram

4 Ronaldo has been with Rodriguez since 2016 Credit: Getty



"He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My co-workers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it," she added.

It wasn't long before she had to quit her job at the store because of crowding.

But their relationship remained strong with Rodriguez taking on the role of parenting the three children Ronaldo had (Cristiano Jr, Eva Maria and Mateo) before meeting her.

Ronaldo and and Rodriguez share two children together, daughters Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda.



Ronaldo must now feel that 'click'

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also revealed during the documentary that he hadn't yet put a ring on Rodríguez's finger because he hadn't felt the special 'click'.

'I always tell her, 'when we get that click'. Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about," Ronaldo said.

4 Rodriguez been by Ronaldo's side over the last ten years with their life currently in Saudi Arabia Credit: Getty

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'



At the same time, Rodríguez admitted that her friends would always joke with her about when the wedding was.

"They're always joking about the wedding. 'When is the wedding?'" Rodríguez said.

"Since Jennifer Lopez's song The Ring or When came out, they started singing it to me. And well, this is not up to me."

Now it's finally happened.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement, Aston Villa line up move for West Ham star while Newcastle press on with pursuit of Benfica defender: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea sign Marc Cucurella replacement

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal for a fee of around £16.3m plus add-ons.

The 28-year-old replaces Marc Cucurella, who signed for Real Madrid earlier this summer in a £55.8m deal.

After signing his five-year deal, Chavarria told club media: 'I'm so excited to get started.

'This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. This is one of the best days of my life,' added the 28-year-old.

'It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success.

'There are a lot of people who have helped me get to this moment and I have to thank my family. They have always supported me and today is only possible because of them.'

Chelsea have signed Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria on a five-year deal

Toon press on with Benfica target

Newcastle United are pressing ahead with talks to sign Amar Dedic from Benfica.

The 23-year-old right-back played for new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Dedic has been capped 31 times by Bosnia and is valued around £25m.

Newcastle continue to work on a new midfielder too.

Camara never lies

Crystal Palace have held further talks with Monaco over 22-year-old midfielder Lamine Camara.

The clubs have been discussing a £40million deal for the Senegal international who has also been tracked by Chelsea, Newcastle and Manchester United.

Camara impressed in Monaco's friendly against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Monaco are understood to want a fee in excess of £50m who has three years left on contract.

Palace have also spoken about France international Youssouf Fofana who is available from AC Milan.

Villa Wan him

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

The 28-year-old is ready to leave West Ham to stay in the top flight and has been considered as a new addition by a number of clubs including Arsenal but Villa are understood to be in pole position.

The Congo international has also been linked with Everton but manager David Moyes is exploring other options.

Aston Villa are discussing a move for West Ham defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka

Villa are in the process of signing Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid to strengthen their left back options and now Wan-Bissaka looks a strong option for their right-back berth.

They have previously discussed Emerson Royal at Flamengo.

Villa are also finalising a deal to send Evann Guessand on loan to Crystal Palace.

The Eagle has landed... again!

Evann Guessand has rejoined Crystal Palace on a season-long loan from Aston Villa.

Guessand spent the second half of last season on loan at Selhurst Park, playing 14 times as Palace won the UEFA Conference League.

Palace chose not to exercise his option to buy at the end of last season’s loan but remained open to the possibility of Guessand returning on loan. This switch also includes an option to buy.

Palace initially chased the Ivorian on a permanent deal last summer, but he opted to join Aston Villa - where he made just 21 appearances - in a £30million deal from Nice.

Rejoining Palace, Guessand said: ‘I'm so happy to be here. I already have good memories here – but I think it's only the beginning. I hope many more are coming.’

BOBBY MANZI

Spurs youngster heading to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-Hyeok has joined KVC Westerlo in Belgium on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Yang, 20, signed for Spurs in July 2024 but completed the season in South Korea and moved to London in January 2025. He has been on loan at QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry.

Spurs have a close relationship with Westerlo. Alfie Devine and Luka Vuskovic are among those who have been loaned there.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are married! Portugal star ties the knot with influencer in an 'intimate and private' civil ceremony attended by their five children
Sports.content:
Have YOU got a story? Email tips@dailymail.co.uk

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal.

The couple tied the knot in an 'intimate and private' ceremony on Tuesday with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

He captioned the post: 'C❤️G.'

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal attended by their five children

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The wedding news comes just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina.

Then the next month, they announced they were expecting, giving birth to their daughter Alana Martina in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

Join the discussion Do you think celebrity weddings should be private family affairs or public celebrations shared with fans?

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids. Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now who is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: UEFA don't want clubs like Aston Villa to win. They've forced them to sell their best players, as 'bigger' clubs lose hundreds of millions with impunity. But thanks to Unai Emery, Villa are beating the system, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
UEFA don't want clubs like Aston Villa to win. They've forced them to sell their best players, as 'bigger' clubs lose hundreds of millions with impunity. But thanks to Unai Emery, Villa are beating the system, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Forget what European football chiefs might say in public. Aston Villa are unwelcome guests at tonight’s party in Salzburg and the game’s wealthy elite would be perfectly happy if they never turned up again.

If that sounds harsh, read the thoughts of UEFA finance chief Andrea Traverso. Speaking last year about financial rules that seem to reward money-making activities over anything that happens on the pitch, Traverso admitted ‘the regulations were never designed to create competitive balance but rather to bring financial discipline, and that stability is precisely what continues to attract investors to European football’.

In the interview with the Football Benchmark group, Traverso also accepts that ‘if the financial gap between clubs continues to grow, it becomes harder to maintain that competitive balance’. But if that is a priority for UEFA, they have a funny way of showing it.

If they beat Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup tonight, Villa will collect a second European trophy in less than three months, following their Europa League triumph in May. They are about to start their second Champions League campaign in three seasons and under Unai Emery, they have finished seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth in the Premier League. Their progress has been astonishing.

Instead of being able to build on that, Villa have had to sell their best attacker and best midfielder this summer, as well as France’s left back, just to satisfy UEFA’s financial controls.

Their best defender, Ezri Konsa, is wanted by Arsenal and Emery hopes he will not follow Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne through the exit door.

Aston Villa's progress under Unai Emery has been astonishing - and now they have a chance of a second European trophy in three months

But they have been hamstrung by the financial rules of UEFA and the Premier League, leaving them with little choice but to sell star men like Morgan Rogers (pictured)

Even though Villa co-owners Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens are worth a combined £10billion, Villa are effectively being punished because they cannot generate the same revenue as commercial giants like Manchester United, Tottenham and Chelsea.

If Villa qualify for Europe’s top competition again this season, they could start to dream of challenging their richer rivals long-term. If they do, it might just be the greatest achievement of Emery’s top-level career.

Why did Villa have to sell?

Villa were fined about £9.5million a year ago for breaching UEFA regulations and as part of their three-year settlement agreement, they must deliver a progress report to European football chiefs every six to 12 months.

Across last season and this, Villa are allowed to spend up to £52million more than they earn on transfers and wages. That meant that to strengthen this summer, Villa had to sell, and the departures of Rogers, Tielemans and Digne has yielded about £150million.

That Rogers should move to Chelsea, who did not qualify for Europe last season and whose operating losses over the last three years were nearly £700million, is another indicator of how misguided UEFA’s priorities seem to be.

If Villa can balance their books to UEFA’s satisfaction, they will be released from the settlement agreement a year early.

Even then, they will have to keep football spending to 70 per cent of revenue, in line with squad cost ratio rules. Villa plan to expand their stadium to 50,000 and continue to grow commercially, yet their revenue for 2024-25 was still nearly £200million short of the £565million generated by Tottenham, who finished 17th in the top flight last season, and the previous one.

It is a relatively bleak picture for those who like football to be unpredictable. Because if Villa, who finished 14th in Deloitte’s latest football money league with a revenue of £378million, struggle to stay in touch, then what hope is there for smaller or similar-size clubs?

Left back Lucas Digne is now on the books of Villa's opponents tonight, PSG - one of three high-profile exits this summer

What do they do now?

Villa are not blameless here. If they feel they have one hand tied behind their back, it is their fault, too.

Emery has been brilliant since taking control in 2022 but the transfer market is his Achilles heel.

Last summer Villa spent £26million on Evann Guessand and gave high wages to loan players Jadon Sancho and Harvey Elliott. Within a few weeks, Emery had decided he didn’t really fancy any of them.

They paid about £18million on Tammy Abraham last winter but are now open to selling him or letting him leave on loan.

Something happens to Emery when the window is open. Ultra-meticulous in his training sessions and match prep, Emery is less consistent when assessing the market. One week he may decide he wants a right-footed left winger, only to ask for a left-footed right winger the next. Sometimes his emotions get the better of him and this is where the calmness of transfer chief Roberto Olabe should help.

Villa have far less margin of error with deals than their wealthier rivals and they cannot afford more mistakes this summer.

Based on his performances for Freiburg last season and for Switzerland at the World Cup, £52million Johan Manzambi is an exciting signing – but for now he is out with a knee injury and it is unclear when he will return. It would be no surprise if the 20-year-old missed the opening weeks of the season.

For £35million, Joao Gomes looks a solid capture from Wolves for a midfield badly in need of numbers after the sale of Tielemans and Amadou Onana’s ACL injury, while the most fascinating deal so far was Alejandro Garnacho.

For £35million, Joao Gomes looks a solid capture from Wolves for a midfield badly in need of numbers

Alejandro Garnacho is one of the most eye-catching additions of the summer. You sense his early performances will set the tone for his campaign

Villa’s owners have good relations with their Chelsea counterparts and it seems plausible that the Garnacho deal was discussed during negotiations over Rogers' move to Stamford Bridge.

Earlier in the summer, Villa had looked at various options for the wide attacking spots, from Harvey Barnes to Crysencio Summerville and Ibrahim Mbaye, the PSG winger who could feature at the Red Bull Arena.

In the end though they settled on Garnacho, as perhaps was inevitable once it became clear that Rogers would join Chelsea. It has emerged that at least two weeks before the deal was announced, the England international was telling friends he knew he would be moving to Chelsea. Perhaps at that stage, Garnacho also knew his next club, too, and do not rule out Nicolas Jackson making the same trip in the closing hours of the window.

Emery has a mixed record with Manchester United cast-offs. While at Villa for five months in 2025, Marcus Rashford did well enough to earn a loan move to Barcelona. Sancho, on the other hand, made no significant impression.

If Emery did indeed want Garnacho above all other targets, then he may be able to bring the best from him. If there were other priorities at stake, it might be tricker for the Argentine to make an impression. You sense his early performances will set the tone for his campaign.

Is this a refresh?

This is a very different Villa from the one that hammered Freiburg 3-0 to lift the Europa League at the Tupras Stadium in Istanbul.

Not only have Rogers and Tielemans – two of the goalscorers that night – left along with Digne, but Emery’s coaching staff has changed, too.

Austin MacPhee, Villa’s high-profile set-piece coach, has taken his dead-ball strategies and Kurt Cobain hairdo to Chelsea. Emery’s experienced No2 Pako Ayestaran and performance coach Antonio Rodriguez Saravia – known as Rodri – have also moved on. That is six key figures in the Istanbul triumph who are no longer employed by Villa.

It's not just change on the pitch for Villa. Austin MacPhee (right), their high-profile set-piece coach, has taken his dead-ball strategies and Kurt Cobain hairdo to Chelsea

This might not be all bad, though. Working for Emery is exhausting, both for players and staff members.

Emery leads all training sessions and will repeat drills until they are done exactly as he wishes, even physically moving players a centimetre to the left or right until they are standing in the correct spot.

Then there are the tactical meetings in the video room, which usually happen twice a week and can last up to 90 minutes. Not to mention the individual audiences with Emery that players have throughout the season. For staff, hours are long.

Emery’s appetite for work is astonishing, even for a coach earning about £12million per year. Quite simply, the Spaniard does not switch off and that means his key deputies are always on call. Perhaps only Marcelo Bielsa and Pep Guardiola have a similar 24/7 approach and that is not easy for their lieutenants. Chema Sanz and Pal Fjelde, the new set-piece coach, are next in line to face the Emery whirlwind.

These changes might work for the best, though. Last season was a supreme effort from all involved, especially given the chaos of last August.

It is doubtful whether they could repeat it. Perhaps the changes in personnel will bring fresh energy. For Gomes, Manzambi, Fjelde and others, Emery’s methods are new and exciting. Adding another trophy would be the perfect start to the new era.

Sports.title: Roberto Martinez 'holds talks to become Netherlands' new manager in what would be his THIRD international job following Portugal failure - after ex-Liverpool boss Arne Slot pulled out of the running
Sports.content:
Roberto Martinez has emerged as a shock candidate to become the new Netherlands manager, as their search continues for Ronald Koeman's successor.

The Dutch have been on the lookout for a new boss after Koeman resigned following their World Cup last-32 penalty shootout exit by Morocco in June.

And according to De Telegraaf, the KNVB (the Royal Dutch Football Association) have turned their sights towards Martinez.

They report that technical director Nigel de Jong has held talks with the 53-year-old about taking the reins.

If the Spaniard was to join he would become the Netherlands' first foreign manager in 48 years - since Austrian Ernst Happel led them to the 1978 World Cup final, where they lost 3-1 to Argentina.

De Telegraaf note that Martinez is a close friend of Jordi Cruyff and a supporter of the iconic football philosophy of his late father, Johan.

Roberto Martinez has reportedly held talks with the Netherlands over becoming their new boss

The Dutch on the hunt for a new manager since Ronald Koeman (centre) resigned in June

Martinez resigned as Portugal boss after their World Cup last-16 exit by Spain in July

If Martinez did get the job it would be his third foray in international management having been in charge of Belgium and Portugal previously. However, despite having star-studded squads at his disposal both tenures ended in disappointment.

He achieved a third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup with Belgium but they crashed out in the group stages four years later. Then with Portugal, he won the 2024-25 Nations League but lost 1-0 to eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this summer's World Cup.

After that defeat, Martinez resigned from the role in July as pressure grew over his tactics and team selections.

The Netherlands turning to Martinez, comes after several homegrown managers have turned down the role - including Arne Slot, who wishes to remain in club football for now.

Slot, who left Liverpool at the end of last season, was in negotiations to take over the national team of his homeland but withdrew from the race.

Some reports suggested Slot had turned down the opportunity because of potential salary and contract length, but the 47-year-old has released a statement revealing the true reason.

'Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration,' Slot said via Dutch publication Voetbal International. 'That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks.

'At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team. And why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

'It would be a great honor to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.'

Sports.title: Carabao Cup's weekend kick-off pays off with crowd records smashed - even WITHOUT West Ham's bumper attendance!
Sports.content:
The EFL's decision to start the season with the Carabao Cup appears to have paid off – after record attendances flocked to matches over the weekend.

Last September, Daily Mail Sport revealed that league bosses were considering a break from tradition and kicking off the new campaign with a round of League Cup fixtures, rather than league games.

They were forced to act in the midst of an increasingly pressurised calendar, further complicated by the fact that this September will feature an extended three-week international break which reduces the amount of time to play Carabao Cup games before clubs enter European competition.

And the move has delivered the highest crowd numbers since the current format of the League Cup, which came into play in the 2001-02 season.

A total of 313,852 people attended the first round ties, smashing the previous record of just short of 250,000 set in 2023-24. The staggering attendance of 53,369, recorded at the London Stadium for West Ham United's clash with Portsmouth (which included 9,000 away fans), has had a major impact. However, without that fixture, the record would still have been broken.

There were record attendances at Carabao Cup first round matches at the weekend

The average crowd for this season has been 8,967, while the two previous seasons have been around the 6,000 mark.

And of the 15 sides who had first round fixtures at home last season and did so again this time around, all but three recorded higher gates.

'It has been fantastic to see club football return with such strong support across the opening Carabao Cup fixtures, with supporters once again demonstrating in record numbers the passion, loyalty and commitment that sits at the heart of the EFL, said EFL chief executive Trevor Birch.

'As we look ahead to the start of the league season this weekend, there is a real sense of anticipation across our clubs and their supporters. The opening fixtures have provided an exciting early marker, and we now look forward to a season that will once again show why supporters can 'expect everything' from the EFL.'

Sports.title: These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE

Unlock more from Craig Hope inside the Newcastle camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling.

For a club who want to be among the world's best by 2030, this was an understated arrival for a head coach whose contract takes us through to that date. He is, by that logic, the man the Newcastle hierarchy believe can lead them to the top.

Not that there was any talk of Champions League and Premier League titles here, or questions about signing Kylian Mbappe, as there was at the outset of the Saudi project nearly five years ago. Veteran midfielder Pierre Emile-Hojbjerg, 31, has been the No1 target in recent days.

Rather, this was something of a reality check, and that is no reflection on Jaissle. The German spoke with enthusiasm and intelligence, and he did so alone. There was no sign of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan or hierarchy on stage with the 38-year-old. No global media, either. This is where Newcastle are at right now, and Jaissle appears smart enough to know what he is walking into – a club where the best players and manager have not long walked out.

His demeanour was one of excitement, composure and, a word he sought to stress more than once, optimism. There is a believable authority about him. But beneath the positivity was a more subtle message. He needs new players. And he needs time.

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas. You took note when he was asked about the departures of senior players and responded by referencing a leadership ‘vacuum’. He is right, too.

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas

So, with Bruno Guimaraes now in north London, does he have a new captain yet? ‘No,’ came the reply. And that was that.

His answer when asked what remit the board had given him for this season was equally revealing, given Eddie Howe and the club made no secret of their expectation of European qualification last term, which ended in 12th place in the Premier League.

‘(The remit) is that we are ambitious, but this will not happen overnight, especially when you have such a big transition phase now,’ he said. ‘It makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control. Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful.’

Transition was another word he used repeatedly. In fact, the Newcastle 2.0 that chief executive David Hopkinson has spoken about post-Howe feels, at this moment, more like Newcastle 1.5. Less than two weeks out from the visit of Liverpool in the Premier League opener, Jaissle has no fit full backs, while the experienced midfielder he craves appears no closer to arriving.

‘We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want,’ he said. ‘Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic, but he is another who has never played in England. It is not hard to understand why 97-cap Denmark midfielder Hojbjerg, with more than 250 Premier League appearances at Southampton and Tottenham, was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt. The Marseille midfielder, however, has opted against the move. The optics of Newcastle 1.5 are not the easiest sell.

Because when the target of ‘consolidation’ was put to the manager of this Saudi-owned club at his first press conference – and it did not sound ridiculous or provoke a challenge – it told you plenty about the task in front of him. For that, he deserves patience.

‘It's a big challenge,’ he said. ‘It always is when there's a transition period, but it's not the time to complain. It doesn't make sense to see the negative. We want to see the chance in the situation.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic (left), but he is another who has never played in England

It is not hard to understand why Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (right) was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt

You suspect Jaissle's demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition

There is another challenge for Jaissle – keeping himself out of the stands. Although you suspect a demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition.

At times in Valencia during his first game on Saturday night, it looked like he was making overlapping runs beyond right winger Anthony Elanga. Indeed, he has already asked club staff how many bookings a manager is allowed before they serve a touchline ban, and he returned a hesitant laugh when informed it was just three.

‘I will not change my style because that's my personality,’ said the former Al Hilal boss. ‘On the touchline, I am emotional. But I need to respect the technical box a bit more. I had a long line in Saudi Arabia, so I think my GPS would be quite high! I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little!’

There were other flashes of levity, too, including mention of the song which the Toon Army bestowed on him in Spain – ‘Jaissle, I can boogie’ to the tune of Baccara’s Yes Sir, I Can Boogie. ‘I heard it once and I was smiling,’ he said. ‘The guys around me, all the staff members, said they're really looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let's see about that.’

To sit in the bar and be serenaded will need wins. To get those wins, at least on a consistent enough basis to make a success of his debut season, will need more players of greater experience and quality. He knows that. Maybe it is, then, that a low-key introduction was what was necessary. There is no need for Jaissle to boogie just yet. First, he needs a team to dance with.

Sports.title: GORDON MILNE interview: Coventry's golden age and all the 'daft' schemes of Jimmy Hill, growing up with Bill Shankly, learning from Tom Finney, Japan with Gary Lineker... and how he nearly replaced Shankly as Liverpool manager
Sports.content:
Coventry City were the epitome of fresh thinking and pioneering change when they last broke the surface at the top of English football.

They had been powered to promotion in 1967 with sky blue trains and buses for fans and their players slid behind the wheels of pristine sky blue Rover cars and drove them into Europe on summer tours to blend the city's industrial heritage and fanbase with its flourishing football team. They went on at the vanguard when it came to shirt sponsorship and creative kit designs, all-seater stadiums and electric scoreboards.

And their gravity-defying refusal to kowtow to football's old-world order and simply disappear again prompted jokes that if the Titanic had been painted sky blue it would never have gone down. Coventry remained afloat in the top flight for 34 years and Gordon Milne, the manager for nine of them from 1972, traces all of that back to the influence of Jimmy Hill.

'There was a culture there and it was created by Jimmy,' says Milne, 89 years old and delighted to see Coventry back in the Premier League after 25 years of exile.

'He was a clever guy, intelligent enough to see where football was going. A humble guy, which surprises some people. A lot of people didn't like Jimmy. He'd tell me when he was on Match of the Day how he received thousands of letters telling him to eff off. He used to say his unpopularity kept him in the job.

'At Coventry, he put himself about, went into the factories and connected with people. He loved Coventry and he loved football.'

When Coventry were last promoted to the top flight in 1967 they stayed afloat for 34 years, with nine of them under the management of Gordon Milne

Milne attributes a lot of the success to Jimmy Hill, who led the club from the third tier to the top flight before resigning on the eve of the new season to take a job in television

Hill had been manager of Coventry for six years from 1961. The club was in the third tier when he arrived, and he led them to two promotions before a shock announcement on the eve of their debut season in the old Division One that he intended to quit for a job as head of sport at London Weekend Television.

He certainly knew the future of football would be tied closely to television. When Hill returned in 1975 as managing director and later chairman, Milne was manager and Ron Wylie was his assistant.

'People thought we wouldn't last five minutes once Jimmy was back,' he says. 'We were scratching about near the wrong end of the table with all the journalists writing us off for relegation. Then Jimmy says he wants to meet for a working breakfast. We'd never heard of a working breakfast. Ron, a Glaswegian, says, "Well, that's it, we're on our way".

'It was in a period when Jimmy had investments in developing football in Saudi Arabia and he said, "I want you to help me find a coach". We got talking and the conversation moved onto the salary, which was more than a hundred grand a year and probably about three or four times what I was earning.

'I just remember Ron going: "How much!" Then he said: "We'll do it." And Jimmy laughed and said: "Oh no, no, no… you two are going nowhere." And he knew what he was saying. He knew there had been speculation. That meant a lot to us.'

Bill McGarry, former Ipswich Town and Wolverhampton Wanderers boss, got the lucrative job in charge of Saudi Arabia.

Milne thrived alongside Hill's energy and fearless ambition, unearthing gems in the transfer market, blooding young players alongside carefully selected veterans. In the distinctive Admiral kit, Coventry came seventh in 1977-78. The brown away kit, now portrayed as a cult classic, was rarely worn.

'We hardly won in it,' says Milne. 'The fans were saying it was jinxed but again Admiral came on the scene and wanted to do something different and we were up for it. I only wish I'd kept some of those shirts.'

Milne poses at the launch of the now cult classic brown Admiral kit of the late 1970s

Alongside assistant Ron Wylie (bottom row, fourth from left) with the Coventry squad at the start of the 1975-76 season

Pictured here with Sir Bobby Charlton (left) and Bobby Moore (right), Milne was part of the provisional England 1966 World Cup squad but did not make Sir Alf Ramsey's final cut

Coventry were ahead of their time, and the team was free-scoring, featuring favourites from the era such as winger Tommy Hutchison, a former team-mate of Milne's at Blackpool, and the duo of Mick Ferguson and Ian Wallace up front.

'I always thought if you could score 60 goals you wouldn't be relegated,' says Milne, whose team made a serious effort to beat Nottingham Forest to sign Trevor Francis from Birmingham in Britain's first million-pound transfer in 1979.

'We were very close to signing Trevor. I knew him from the days working with England Under 18s and one of my best pals was Jim Smith, who was manager at Birmingham and absolutely loved Jimmy Hill, so we were in and ready to pay a million for him. It didn't quite work out and going to Forest was the right decision for Trevor, but Jimmy's thinking was, "I'll get Trevor".'

In his study, a shimmering trove of memorabilia, Milne rummages through desk drawers and piles of photographs as he reminisces, pulls books from the shelves and flips through the pages to confirm his recall.

He has a wealth of knowledge accrued from a stellar career which began playing at Preston alongside Tom Finney.

'The best player I've ever seen,' says Milne. 'Outside right, outside left, centre forward, two great feet. He had the art of moving the ball in a flash and shielding it with his body. He'd done it before you knew he was doing it.

'Strong, good in the air. Played through injury. I always picture him on the old treatment room with its immaculate wooden floors, and he'd be on the table, legs black and blue, bruises everywhere and the gaffer would say, "What about tomorrow Tom?" and he'd say, "I'll be OK". Top guy.'

Milne's father Jimmy played for Preston in the pre-war years with Bill Shankly. Both Scottish, their families lived in the same street. As a boy, if Milne Jr ever went outside to kick a ball against the wall, he found Shankly was soon out there kicking it with him.

Bill Shankly (centre) and Bob Paisley (furthest left) attend to Milne (second right) and his Liverpool team-mates on the treatment table

Shankly directs the tactics board in 1963 before an FA Cup quarter-final against West Ham

So perhaps it was no surprise then that Shankly made him one of his first signings as Liverpool boss, in 1960. Two years later, they were drawn in the FA Cup fifth round to play against Preston, where Milne's father had returned as manager.

After two goalless draws, Peter Thompson scored the winner for Preston in a second replay. A year later, Shankly signed Thompson from North End as well. In 1964 his team won the title, a year later the FA Cup and a year later another title. Liverpool would never be the same again.

'What Shanks did at Liverpool was similar to what Jimmy did at Coventry,' says Milne. 'They were both genuine. Jimmy might throw some daft ideas around but he didn't bulls***. They believed in him in Coventry, in the way they believed in Shanks in Liverpool.

'He connected with the people and talked about them. We were doing it for them. Shanks always used to say, "Listen to them". At quarter to three, he would open the dressing room door and say, "The doors have been closed since quarter past two, we can't get another body in the place, how can you let them down? You can't let them down".

'That would be his team talk and when the music scene got going and The Beatles and Gerry and the Pacemakers came on the scene, he built on that. Liverpool was the place to be.'

Milne was considered as a replacement when Shankly quit in 1974. In his second season at Coventry, before the teams met at Highfield Road, he was in conversation with Shankly's assistant Bob Paisley, a man of few words who nodded towards the Liverpool team and said: 'This is a job for you, son.'

Paisley's words made more sense when Shankly quit at the end of the season and Milne was invited to meet Liverpool chairman John Smith and secretary Peter Robinson at a hotel in Manchester.

'What I should've said, that I never said, was that I'd love the job and would've walked up the M6 for it, and that if I got it, I'd want Bob as my right-hand man,' says Milne. 'Bob could read a game. He was brilliant. Perfect for Shanks. They were the perfect combination and Shanks listened to him. He'd pretend he didn't, but he did.

Winning the FA Cup at Wembley in 1965 (Milne pictured centre in tracksuit)

Milne (bottom row, third from left) with the 1966-67 Liverpool team, captained by Ron Yeats, and their First Division and Charity Shield titles

'The worry for Bob was being the No1 man. He didn't want the publicity. Bob took it, but he didn't want it.'

Milne's book, published by Pitch in 2023, was titled Shankly, My Dad and Me. He had sought Shankly's advice when he was offered the Coventry job.

Milne, then in charge of non-League Wigan, was interviewed by Coventry chairman Derrick Robbins on the backseat of his Rolls-Royce. Robbins wanted to recreate Joe Mercer's success with Malcolm Allison at Manchester City by bringing in Mercer as general manager and Milne as manager, in what today we would recognise as the roles of director of football and head coach.

Shankly summoned Milne to Blackpool, where he was on his summer holiday.

The Liverpool boss, wearing pyjamas and with his face smothered in Vaseline, answered the door to his hotel room and invited Milne to step inside before asking only one question: 'Do they want Milne or do they want Mercer?'

Milne explained that Coventry wanted both. 'Aye, but do they want Milne or do they want Mercer?' repeated Shankly.

Milne said he believed they wanted Milne. 'Take it then,' advised Shankly, then asked him to leave because his wife Nessie was sleeping next door.

Milne spent a decade at Highfield Road, the final year as director of football before leaving in 1982 for Leicester, where he won promotion and unearthed another prolific strike partnership in Alan Smith and Gary Lineker in his ongoing quest for 60 goals a season.

Milne and Coventry general manager Joe Mercer greet the team ahead of the 1972-73 season

At his unveiling as Besiktas director of football in 2005, after a highly successful period as manager when he led the club to three consecutive titles from 1990 to 1992

When Coventry won the FA Cup in 1987, the only major trophy of their 143-year existence, he was moving to Istanbul, where he guided Besiktas to a hat-trick of Turkish titles. They did not lose as they won the third and Milne is a legend there.

Lineker lured him to Nagoya Grampus Eight in Japan for a year before a return to Turkish football and a spell as Newcastle's director of football with Sir Bobby Robson.

Coventry though has always been close to his heart and he is proud of his part in the legacy. 'Nine years and we didn't get relegated,' he says. 'You couldn't say that's the objective at the start of every season but over those nine seasons, look at who went down. Some big ones went.'

Among them Manchester United, Chelsea twice and Tottenham. And, like many others, Milne was thrilled when Frank Lampard led the Sky Blues once more into the Premier League.

'Frank has done a great job,' says Milne. 'He has done it all as a player, knows his football and has strong contacts. It looks like they want to play for him and that's important. And he has connected with the fans. It's great to see them back.'

Now to see if they can defy gravity all over again.

Sports.title: Britain's new golden girl: Cambridge English Grad-turned sprinter Amy Hunt who went to Margaret Thatcher's old school wins 100m at European Athletics Championships
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

She became the fastest woman in Europe on Monday night, when she won a gold medal for sprinting 100m in 11 seconds.

Yet that's not the only honour Amy Hunt, 24, has earned - with a degree in English Literature from the University of Cambridge under her belt too.

And although she is a fellow old girl of the same grammar school as fellow high-achiever Margaret Thatcher, she has also retained the ability to very much let her hair down.

For despite reaching the pinnacles of success on the track and the classroom, her social media accounts are full of pictures of her enjoying more than the odd glass of wine.

Miss Hunt said after winning the women's 100m final at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham on Monday: 'I want it all, and I think I'm someone who doesn't shy away from what she knows she can do.

'I knew I could come away with a gold coming into the day.

'I had such a big premonition, and I just love my job. This is what makes it the best.

'My first gold. I think it was definitely time for an upgrade.'

Miss Hunt, who evidently enjoys a night out, poses while watching a Taylor Swift concert

She then studied at Corpus Christi college, Cambridge - financing her studies with earnings from track events and sponsors

Glasses of wine are a regular fixture on Miss Hunt's social media feeds

She also finds the time between training sessions to carefully curate her warbrobe

Miss Hunt poses with a bottle of wine during her Cambridge years

It was Miss Hunt's first gold after winning the women's 100m final at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham

Miss Hunt, 5ft10ins, had previously won English Schools races at the Birmingham track, but her gold is her first major victory. It makes her a big hope for 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. She is actually considered better at 200m.

Raised in Newark, she attended Mrs Thatcher's grammar, Kesteven and Grantham Girls' School, like the former Premier studying chemistry at A Level. She played cello too.

Miss Hunt then studied at Corpus Christi college, Cambridge - financing her studies with earnings from track events and sponsors.

Upon graduating two years ago she joked: 'I just got one degree hotter.'

She had herself into student social events too, posing in a party dress and with a bottle of wine for one picture.

Miss Hunt has also repeatedly posed with glasses of wine and other drinks in sun-baked squares and in a bikini in an infinity pool.

She currently lives and trains a 20-minute train ride from Venice - and is feasting her eyes on Italian art.

The Renaissance woman said last year her current motto is 'Medals before men', but was not down about it, adding: 'My two little legs have left me living the life of my dreams.'

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Man Utd's £14m move, midfielder 'spotted' at Liverpool, Lewis-Skelly move off
Sports.content:
The latest Arsenal, Liverpool, Man Utd transfer news and updates from around the Premier League as the window enters its final stretch ahead of the new season

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog for Wednesday, August 12. With around three weeks remaining, the window is entering its final stretch for Manchester United, Liverpool and more to get deals over the line.

Arsenal have been busy so far this summer, adding Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis but failing to land Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid. The Gunners remain linked to Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, and versatile youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly is said to have been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United.

The Red Devils completed some fast deals to bring midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos to the club, but could still add another. They remain linked to Lewis Hall as Michael Carrick wants to strengthen his full-back options, and could also sign a striker if the opportunity arises.

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Ronald Araujo to bolster Andoni Iraola's defence, having signed Spain star Victor Munoz earlier in the month. All eyes are on whether they can get a deal done for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola before the deadline, however.

Join us for updates on those clubs and more as we take in the latest transfer news and rumours from the Premier League and Europe.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest

Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham, with the final stages of transfer negotiations progressing following interest from Arsenal, Inter Milan and Barcelona

View 2 Images Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA via Getty Images)

Cristian Romero is poised to join Atletico Madrid after the Spanish side agreed to pay £34million for the Tottenham captain. Romero has attracted interest from Arsenal, Inter Milan and Barcelona, but will join Diego Simeone's side this summer.

The 28-year-old has always appeared likely to leave Spurs this summer following the arrivals of Marcos Senesi and John Paul van Hecke from Bournemouth and Brighton respectively.

His availability has sparked plenty of interest, with Tottenham's north London rivals Arsenal even contacting his representatives to discuss the possibility of the most controversial transfer in recent Premier League history.

Inter Milan appeared to be the other most likely destination for the Argentina international. The Italian giants have agreed a £34m fee with Spurs, but not personal terms with the centre-back.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Atletico Madrid always seemed like the perfect fit for Romero, whose playing style suits his compatriot and soon-to-be manager Diego Simeone. Almost everything has now been agreed, according to reports in Spain, and the deal will go ahead.

The deal will bring to a close the possibility of him following in the footsteps of Sol Campbell and William Gallas by moving between Arsenal and Tottenham. The Gunners enquired about his availability in their search for defensive reinforcements following the news that William Saliba will miss the start of the season due to a back injury.

Arsenal have also been linked with Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa and Barcelona's Jules Kounde. And a move for Kounde could rely on Tottenham, with Barcelona reportedly targeting Spurs' Pedro Porro as their preferred replacement for the Frenchman.

View 2 Images Cristian Romero hasn't returned to Tottenham since the World Cup (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Romero was handed the captain's armband and signed a new four-year contract with Spurs last summer. Speaking on the weekend, manager Roberto De Zerbi kept his cards close to his chest, insisting Romero was still planning to return to Spurs following an extended break after the World Cup.

"I texted with Cuti yesterday to make a plan for when he comes back to London," De Zerbi told reporters in Sydney. "[I did not speak to him about] the transfer market. That's not my job. I know there are many solutions in the transfer market."

Tottenham have invested heavily in the summer transfer window after narrowly escaping relegation to the Championship. Van Hecke and Senesi have been joined by big-money moves for Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, while Andy Robertson has also arrived on a free transfer.

While money has been banked through the departures of Luka Vuskovic, Will Lankshear and Manor Solomon, Spurs still need some more departures, like Romero, to balance the books.

Sports.title: Jeremy Clarkson offered pub for FREE by F1 legend - but there's a catch
Sports.content:
Jeremy Clarkson offered pub for FREE by F1 legend - but there's a catch

Jeremy Clarkson has been a regular on our TV screens for decades, and the former Top Gear presenter was offered a pub for free by F1 legend David Coulthard

View 2 Images Jeremy Clarkson was offered the chance to own another pub (Image: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard has revealed that he offered Jeremy Clarkson the chance to own his pub for free. However, Coulthard did have one condition for the former Top Gear presenter, who is seeing his farming show continue to rise in popularity.

‌



Clarkson’s Farm on Amazon Prime has recently seen season five be released, with the former Grand Tour host‘s latest business venture regularly featured. Clarkson already owns a pub in Oxfordshire, The Farmer’s Dog, which opened in August 2024, and it seems that the 66-year-old had another opportunity to have another business venture.

‌



Coulthard, who was an F1 driver for McLaren in the 1990s and 2000s, has spoken about the decision to own a pub in London. The 55-year-old went on to reveal that he offered the establishment, The Brown Dog, situated in south-west London, to Clarkson at no cost whatsoever, but with a single condition.

‌



Max Verstappen told blunt truth about his F1 career as Red Bull quit decision looms READ MORE :

In a drive-along interview with Jodie Kidd on YouTube, Coulthard said: "I bought a pub in Barnes which just didn't work. It was The Brown Dog, and we couldn't make it work."

The former F1 driver added: "I actually offered it to Jeremy Clarkson. I said, 'Jeremy, I'll give you the pub.

"It's yours, title deeds, but if and when you make money, you start cutting us in.'" Coulthard went on to reveal that Clarkson declined his offer to take ownership of the pub.

‌



View 2 Images The Brown Dog pub, owned by David Coulthard, which was offered to Jeremy Clarkson (Image: tagvenue)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I think it was just too far from where he lives to make it sensible,” Coulthard said. “It's a difficult business."

‌



Clarkson co-hosted The Grand Tour on Amazon alongside Richard Hammond and James May until 2024, when the trio chose to walk away from the hugely popular show.

Since stepping back from his role hosting the motoring adventure programme, Clarkson has become a familiar face on his Amazon farming series, Clarkson's Farm, which follows life at his Diddly Squat Farm in the Cotswolds.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club

Paul Pogba is now understood to be on the lookout for a new team, despite reports claiming the ex-Manchester United midfielder was offered a deal

View 3 Images Paul Pogba's future is uncertain (Image: DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United ace Paul Pogba is on the verge of having his contract torn up by Monaco. Last summer, he signed a two-year contract with the European heavyweights.

However, he may be set for a several month long absence after suffering a hamstring injury during Monaco's recent pre-season tour at St George's Park. It's a huge setback for the World Cup winner, having been handed a four-year ban in February 2024, only for it to be successfully appealed and reduced to 18 months.

Last season, he made six appearances for Monaco and was also in the squad for their recent 3-2 pre-season friendly victory over Liverpool. Now it's being reported the deal may be cancelled.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Athletic understands both club and player are in talks about having his contract mutually terminated. Last summer, he put pen to paper on a two-year deal, before going on to make his first football appearance for 26 months the following November.

Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

In total, Pogba has featured just six times for Monaco, with all of those performances coming in Ligue 1 last season. He was also present at Anfield for his side's 3-2 victory over Liverpool on Sunday.

However, he has been absent throughout Monaco's pre-season due to fitness concerns, and with contract termination talks ongoing, his future at the club looks increasingly uncertain, reports the Manchester Evening News. Last month, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro cast doubt over Pogba's future, suggesting he could depart this summer.

View 3 Images Pogba mase his first appearance in over two years last season (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

"Maybe he'll leave, yes, maybe he'll stay here, yes," Scuro told a news conference. "That's [Pogba's future] a very complicated subject because we have a lot of respect for Paul. For the person first of all.

"When he first arrived here he was very positive, he worked, he helped the young players. But the truth is that the project didn't go well last season. When we started this project during the summer, the expectations that we had were different to what happened.

"I think now, we must be fair to him, look at his preparation every week, to see how he has progressed, his physical level, his technical level. And after, that will be a decision for the coach. If the coach decides to give him game time or not. That depends completely on performances. We have the summer to see what Paul's level will be.

View 3 Images Pogba's future has been plunged into more uncertainty (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"With Paul, the relationship has always been open, transparent. If, at a certain time, the player's objectives and the club's are different, we have to talk and find a solution. Performance will give all the answers we need."

Pogba, who rose through the academy at United, returned to Old Trafford for £89.3million in 2016 following a stint at Juventus. He subsequently became a key player for Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer throughout his six-year second spell with the Reds, racking up more than 200 appearances along the way.

However, Pogba would eventually depart United for a second time in 2022 when his contract ran out, subsequently rejoining Juventus.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'

Newcastle have undergone a major overhaul this summer, with Matthias Jaissle taking over from Eddie Howe as manager and a series of key players leaving in the transfer window

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle offered a heavy does of realism (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has tempered expectations around his side this season in his first press conference after taking over from Eddie Howe.

‌



Jaissle has inherited into a tricky situation on Tyneside following a succession of high-profile exits. Howe walked away after nearly five years in the hot seat, while Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes were sold and Kieran Trippier also departed.

‌



Newcastle banked nearly £250million from those transfers, but have opted to sign young unproven players with potential as replacements. Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure, Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Lukas Hornicek have arrived to work under Jaissle.

‌



The 38-year-old German was hired from Al-Ahli and is under no illusions over the task facing him. "We are in that transition phase," he said. "The players who have left were great characters, great players, experienced players. This is now a vacuum.

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

"We have to adjust something in the squad by signing these profile of players, or other players need to step up and fill these positions and these leadership roles.

"We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want. Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions."

‌



Newcastle saw a move for Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg fall through recently and remain on the lookout for experience in the transfer window.

The Magpies finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season under Howe and Jaissle has refused to state their ambitions this season. "This will not happen overnight, especially when you now have such a big transition phase," he said.

View 3 Images Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes left for Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



"You need to have a clear goal of where we want to go to. Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, then I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now. We can only do our best day by day, breaking it down with the goal long ahead.

"We are ambitious. But it makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control.

"Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful."

‌



View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle has a rebuilding job on his hands (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Jaissle will be a contrast to the reserved Howe on the touchline, with his animated style likely to come to the fore. "I will not change my style because that's my personality," he said.

"On the touchline, I am emotional, but I need to respect the box [technical area] a bit more. I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little. I need to learn that.

Article continues below

"I had a long touchline in Saudi Arabia, so I think the GPS would be quite high if I had worn it!"
