Sports.title: Spotlight: How Monaco GP boss used sand trucks to beat Ecclestone | Brief
Sports.content:
As president of the Automobile Club de Monaco, Michel Boeri has been responsible for securing the future of Formula 1’s most famous race for over 50 years.

Before Liberty Media took over F1, that meant dealing with Bernie Ecclestone. In the seventies, Ecclestone ran the Formula One Constuctors’ Association, which negotiated on behalf of teams (a majority of which were British) with race promoters.

According to Boeri, Ecclestone’s uncompromising tactics required a firm response, as in one case soon after he took over as ACM president in 1972.

“Ecclestone was British, and he was a businessman. I was a rookie,” Boeri told Nice-Matin. “On the eve of the race, he told me: ‘Since we can’t agree on the fee, we’re going on strike.’

“There was no paddock yet, and the teams were based in the Portier parking lot. I called the Spada company and had the exits blocked with sand trucks. Then I went to Ecclestone and told him: ‘You don’t want to race? Fine. Then you’re not getting out.’ That got negotiations moving immediately.”

Boeri’s tactics achieved the desired result – though he also had the police ready to intervene.

“Ecclestone was a man of his word,” he said. “So I went down to the British camp to sign an agreement. There were no lawyers. It was simply: ‘I promise to move the trucks, and you promise to race. Signed, with love.’

“Being very brave, I had still called the police commander beforehand to tell him the British were drunk and aggressive, and to intervene if things got out of hand.

“I handed the paper to Ecclestone, he signed it, and I dropped to one knee. They took it the wrong way and thought a fight was about to break out. Then the cavalry charged! [laughs] It was ridiculous, but we weren’t writing a manual on diplomacy. You went on instinct. You felt your way through it.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Seven possible championship outcomes | Brief
Sports.content:
How is the championship fight most likely to turn out over the remaining races? Steve Rogers assesses the chances of each of the leading drivers.

I can see several different scenarios:

50% – The balance of performance is largely unchanged from the fist half of the season and Kimi wins (covers just holding on to domination).

20% – McLaren’s Zandvoort updates confirm them as the car to beat and Norris puts in a champion’s display to defend his title.

10% – Ferrari find a consistent window and become the car to beat but ‘Ferrari’ it away with mistakes and baffling strategies (Kimi wins)

8% – Ferrari find a consistent window and become the car to beat and Hamilton continues his first half form to win

Sports.title: Lindblad vs Lawson: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson has finally begun what looks like being his first complete season with the same team and the stability appears to be paying off.

Having spent most of last season at Racing Bulls, Lawson has been a regular in the points. He has helped put the team fifth in the standings, on course for what would be its strongest championship finish in any of its guises.

But newcomer Arvid Lindblad has acquitted himself extremely well and goes into the summer break having tapped a strong vein of form. He’s scored in each of the last six grands prix and out-qualified Lawson in the last three – by decent margins, too.

So while Lawson’s numbers look good at the moment, he can’t be complacent about the growing threat on the other side of the Racing Bulls garage. Max Verstappen has all the reasons he needs to jump ship at the top team and if Lawson has a realistic chance of returning he needs to ensure he is the obvious choice. That won’t be the case as long as Lindblad keeps out-qualifying him.

As is often the case at Red Bull’s junior team, there is also pressure from below. Red Bull’s Nikola Tsolov leading the Formula 2 standings in his rookie campaign and the team will surely already be thinking about when he will be ready for a shot at F1.

Honda will introduce a ‘spec 2’ version of its RA626H power unit at the Dutch Grand Prix. The Japanese manufacturer is racing to catch up with its rivals after experiencing serious problems with vibration and insufficient power at the start of the sesason.

Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Answers Devin Haney’s IBF Call
Sports.content:
“Have the WBO.. I want the IBF,” Devin said on X.

Haney seems to have signaled his preferred opponent without directly naming him. The choice makes sense. Paro brings a large following in Australia and the potential for a PPV event built around two welterweight champions.

That separates Paro from Jack Catterall, another opponent who has been discussed for Haney. Catterall presents a difficult fight with his movement, defense, timing and awkward southpaw style.

Paro is a southpaw as well, but he’s much more willing to engage and turn fights into physical exchanges. Haney has generally performed well against aggressive fighters who come forward, giving him opportunities to box from range, counter, and tie up when they get inside.

Catterall offers a different challenge. He’s unlikely to chase Haney recklessly or provide the type of pressure that allows Haney to settle into his preferred rhythm. Taking that fight would mean accepting considerable stylistic difficulty without getting another world title in return.

Paro gives Haney the opportunity to unify the division while bringing an established Australian audience to the promotion. From Haney’s perspective, that combination makes the matchup easier to understand commercially.

Nothing has been finalized, but the exchange leaves little mystery about their interest. Both champions have publicly opened the door to putting the IBF and WBO titles together.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Silences Yvon Durelle in Montreal Rematch
Sports.content:
The rematch drew 11,555 spectators, generating a gate of $140,519 to set a Montreal boxing record. Former world heavyweight champion Jack Sharkey served as referee.

Moore, already well into his 40s, had held the light heavyweight crown since defeating Joey Maxim in December 1952. Durelle, 29, remained a leading contender after his ferocious effort in their initial meeting.

Rather than trading immediately with the heavy-handed challenger, Moore fought cautiously through the opening two rounds. His defense limited Durelle’s opportunities to land the kind of power shots that had caused so much trouble in their first fight.

Two judges had Moore in front after two rounds, while the third had the fight even.

Moore changed the fight completely in the third. A hard right hand dropped Durelle, who beat the count at seven and tried to fight back. The champion quickly closed in.

Three more knockdowns followed as Moore connected with rights and lefts. After the fourth knockdown of the round, Sharkey counted Durelle out at 2:52.

Moore had turned a rivalry born from one of the greatest scares of his championship reign into a decisive three-round knockout.

Durelle faced difficult circumstances before the fight. A boating accident left him with a back injury, and his hometown of Baie-Sainte-Anne suffered the tragic Escuminac Disaster in June, when 35 fishermen lost their lives.

Moore continued his remarkable run near the top of the sport. Durelle later challenged George Chuvalo for the Canadian heavyweight title in November 1959, losing by knockout in the 12th round.

The two rivals eventually became friends. Moore retained enormous respect for Durelle, remembering him as one of the hardest punchers and toughest opponents he faced.

Their first fight became the classic. On August 12, 1959, Moore made the rematch his answer.

Sports.title: Teofimo: Turki Alalshikh Pushed Benn, Ryan Garcia Wanted Me
Sports.content:
“Conor and Ryan are fighting because it’s a Turki thing. Turki pushed that fight,” Teofimo said to Fighthype. “It wasn’t something that Ryan wanted. Ryan wanted to fight me, but, you know, it’s a business at the same time.”

Ryan has since named Lopez among the opponents he wants to face after Benn, along with Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. That shows the interest is there, although it doesn’t establish how close Garcia and Lopez were to actually fighting.

Teofimo has his own fight to win first. He challenges WBA welterweight champion Romero on August 22 in Las Vegas, attempting to capture a title in a third weight division.

Wins by Garcia and Lopez would leave both operating at 147 pounds with a marketable fight available between them. Teofimo would also own the WBA belt, giving Garcia another reason to pursue the matchup.

Garcia has mentioned Romero as a possible opponent as well, meaning Rolly could put himself in position for a rematch if he defeats Lopez.

Lopez believes money and promotional relationships are increasingly determining which fights get made.

“Everybody’s right now more on the money side,” Lopez said. “Everybody’s associated with somebody. Takeover is on his own with his own.”

Teofimo is coming off his January loss to Shakur Stevenson and will be making his welterweight debut against Romero. Rolly already owns a decision victory over Garcia, giving Teofimo a chance to strengthen his case for a Garcia fight with an impressive performance on August 22.

Sports.title: Raymond Muratalla Ready for 140, Targets Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
“I felt the effects of just like the weight cut. Didn’t feel my strongest. Everything wasn’t on point like it usually is,” said Muratalla to ProBox TV.

Moving up five pounds is what Muratalla wants next, although nothing has been finalized with Top Rank.

“That’s one thing I’m looking forward to. I’ve started to feel that in the ring. So I think it’s about that time to move up and feel a lot better and perform a lot better, too.”

Muratalla described making 135 as difficult and said it has “never been easy.” Competing at 140 should make the physical demands easier and allow him to perform closer to his best.

Stevenson is the major target. Muratalla has wanted the fight before, and moving into the light welterweight division would give him another opportunity to pursue it.

“I think it only makes sense now. Something we’ve been wanting and just never goes through. I think at this point, that’d be something that the fans would love to see.”

Muratalla believes his adaptability would give Stevenson a different test from his previous opponents.

“He’s never faced a fighter like me. I think it’s going to put out a good fight for the boxing fans. It’s definitely a fight that’s going to be competitive, a challenging fight and something that boxing needs.”

No decision has been announced regarding Muratalla’s IBF lightweight title, and he said there is no plan yet for his next fight. His preference, however, is clear: move to 140 and pursue the biggest fights available.

If Stevenson isn’t available, Muratalla wants the other champions in the division.

“Mostly champions. That’s all I really want. Whoever is champion, that’s what I’m going to be looking at and headed for.”

Sports.title: Ben Shalom Goes Nuclear On Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
“I’m disgusted by the organization. I can’t say anything more than being disgusted. They don’t care about boxing. They don’t care about British fighters. They don’t care about the sport. They care about profitability for their shareholders and ripping the sport from this country, changing it, packaging it up and excluding everyone else,” said Shalom to talkSPORT Boxing.

Shalom also challenged the British Boxing Board of Control to “get a backbone” and stand against Zuffa’s plans. He feels the UK government would support the regulator if it does.

He views Zuffa as more than another rival bidding for talent. Shalom maintains its attempt to create a separate boxing ecosystem threatens small-hall shows, independent operators, and the traditional pipeline through area, British, and world titles.

Simon Jordan questioned the timing of the outrage, arguing that the promoter’s voice grew louder only after talent contracted to BOXXER began appearing on other platforms.

Jordan also pointed out that British promoters eagerly welcomed Turki Alalshikh before Alalshikh became involved with Zuffa’s boxing operation.

Shalom insisted contractual disputes remain separate issues to handle through the courts. His larger concern involves the prospect of one entity gaining enough power to determine who receives title shots.

The rhetoric was extreme, but the power struggle underneath it is clear. Zuffa is competing with established promoters for fighters, influence, and control over how championship opportunities are distributed.

Ghana News.title: Wa East Assembly commits GH¢2.3m to classroom projects in Katua, Goripie
Ghana News.content:
The Wa East District Assembly has handed over sites for the construction of educational infrastructure valued at about GH¢2.3 million in the Katua and Goripie communities.

The projects comprise a fully furnished three-unit classroom block at Katua and a two-unit kindergarten block at Goripie.

District Chief Executive for Wa East, Adamu Sayibu, said the projects form part of efforts to address infrastructure deficits in the district and improve teaching and learning.

“What we have done today is a great achievement for the education sector,” Mr Sayibu said during the sod-cutting ceremony.

“We have purposefully selected to go to our communities, meet our community members, the landowners, the chiefs, the assembly members, and all the stakeholders, so that collectively we can get befitting lands for educational infrastructure.”

According to the DCE, the Katua project, funded through the District Assemblies Common Fund, will cost approximately GH¢1.5 million and will include a mechanised borehole to provide reliable access to water.

The Goripie kindergarten block, estimated at GH¢750,000, is expected to replace an existing structure which Mr Sayibu described as unsuitable for early childhood education.

The Wa East Human Resource Director of the Ghana Education Service, Mohammed Damba Issah, said congestion remained a major challenge, particularly at Katua Junior High School, which does not have a dedicated classroom block and currently shares limited space with the primary school.

Mr Issah also commended the Member of Parliament for the area, Dr Godfred Seidu Jasaw, for supporting education in the district.

“I have witnessed different types of support from the MP. Be it renovation of classrooms, putting up a classroom block, helping us to organise mock exams, providing learning materials, and the list is very long,” he said.

He appealed to the community to support efforts to renovate older school facilities, including through the mobilisation of PTA dues.

Projects to include improved safety and sanitation

Wa East District Deputy Engineer Isaac Lawerh said the new facilities would go beyond classroom construction and would include modern KVIPs, changing rooms, headteachers’ offices and specialised hexagonal furniture for kindergarten pupils.

“The whole facility is gated. Meaning, if our children enter the school compound and it's locked, they can't go out until school closes,” Mr Lawerh said, highlighting the safety features of the design.

The contractor handling the Katua project, Abubakari Suleman Wataara of LL&K Company Limited, pledged to deliver quality work ahead of the Assembly’s six-month completion schedule.

“For us, we don't do shoddy work,” he said.

He added that, barring major disruptions from the rainy season, the company hoped to complete the project within three months.

“We can assure you that within three months, God willing, if nothing happens, this place will be ready for handover,” Mr Wataara said.

Community pledges support

Assembly Member for Katua, Jatoe Osman, welcomed the project and assured the contractor of the community’s cooperation and support.

“Education is very key to every development, and Katua is no exception,” he said.

Mr Osman said traditional leaders had already made land available for the school project as well as for sand winning to support construction.

“We will put all the checks and balances in place to ensure that the contractor will have a very good environment to be able to do his work,” he added.

The projects are expected to help ease congestion, improve the learning environment and expand access to basic education infrastructure in the two communities.

Ghana News.title: Brother of man trapped under rubble in Colombian quake clings on to hope
Ghana News.content:
Efraín Gallego does not lose faith that his brother will be found alive, although when he speaks about him, trapped beneath the rubble of a building, his voice breaks and he swallows hard until he regains his composure.

"You feel anguish. Every time there is an alert about someone being alive, hope is reborn that we will find him," Gallego tells me emotionally.

His 80-year-old brother was buried along with his wife when the Torres del Limonar building collapsed in Cali.

This city in south-western Colombia is one of the hardest hit by the earthquake.

The building has become a symbol of the tragedy in the country's third most populous city.

Cali has more than two million inhabitants. According to Mayor Alejandro Éder, there are at least 95 dead.

Under the scorching heat on Tuesday morning, Torres del Limonar is a shattered mountain of rubble, with mattresses, furniture, and belongings peeking out from the concrete.

On top of the remains are rescuers and volunteers: "Silence! We are firefighters. If you can hear us, shout or make any noise."

The phrase is repeated every time the teams dig deep enough to believe they may be close to a survivor.

These are the moments when Gallego regains hope, but the seconds pass and no answers come from below.

Torres del Limonar is one of more than 50 collapsed buildings in Cali.

It is located in its south, in the Capri neighbourhood. The four-storey building held dozens of apartments. The exact number of tenants who were inside when it collapsed is unknown.

Around it, apart from some cracks, the rest of the buildings seem to have escaped the fate of the Torres.

Rescuers, military personnel, volunteers, paramedics, firefighters, humanitarian workers, and journalists have come here.

There are more than 100 people waiting for news. According to Mayor Éder, as of Monday night, it was estimated that 25 people were trapped under the rubble.

Éder declared a nighttime curfew to speed up rescue operations.

The night passed. Excavations continue. A rescuer at the site said about 10 people had been saved since the collapse.

Reports in local media, such as one from Blu Pacífico radio, spoke of six survivors up until a few minutes before my arrival, including an infant only a few months old.

In the midst of tragedy, figures are often closer to estimates than definitive data.

"What I can tell you is that right now there are at least two people detected alive. Tunnels are being made to get them out. One of them has to have his leg freed," rescuer James Velasco tells me.

The magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck Colombia on Monday, 10 August, is the worst in this century, according to the National Geological Service.

In addition to Cali, it left destruction and death in other regions such as Chocó, in the north-west.

Around the remains of Torres del Limonar, unlike Gallego, many residents choose not to speak. They are visibly affected.

Some sleep exhausted on the ground or on a sofa placed in the street. Others gather together under the shade for support.

The hours are long, increasingly so, and the anguish grows.

Velasco offers hope.

"In the past I have participated in operations where we have pulled out survivors after seven days trapped."

"Those who are meant to survive, survive. Nothing is written," he adds.

"I wanted to help from the very beginning."

Amid his anguish, Gallego wants to acknowledge the work of ordinary citizens.

"We must mention all the people who have come to help with water, supplies, tools, equipment; there is a lot of collaboration. Volunteers are plentiful," he says.

Alejandro Mahecha, 19, is one of those volunteers. He decided to come after spending the night safely with his family and overcoming the initial shock.

"I wanted to help from the very beginning. The earthquake affected my city and the homes of people I know. I came to this site because there has been a lot of talk about this building and the need for help here," the young man explains.

Together with several friends, Mahecha helps remove rubble, bring water to rescuers, and clear the street to facilitate evacuation efforts.

In the background, hammers and saws can be heard creating escape routes through the destruction.

They stop only when those present raise their arms.

That means everyone must remain silent. Gallego waits. This time, too, there was no news of his brother.

Ghana News.title: Bondi Beach shooting hero’s assault charges dropped by police
Ghana News.content:
A man who was hailed a hero for disarming one of the Bondi Beach shooters in December has had assault charges against him dropped by police.

Ahmed al Ahmed was charged in June with domestic violence common assault, as well as stalking and intimidation, after an alleged incident with his father in March at a home in southwest Sydney. Ahmed denied both charges.

On Wednesday, in a local Sydney court, prosecutors withdrew the charges after it was agreed that Ahmed would abide by an apprehended domestic violence order for 12 months, limiting his contact with his father.

Outside the court, Ahmed, 44, welcomed the development, telling reporters that he was a "free man" and that he hoped for "peace".

Defence lawyer Mohamed Sakr said in court that the order prohibiting Ahmed from assaulting, threatening, stalking or intimidating his father had been accepted without admissions, according to national broadcaster ABC.

Ahmed made global headlines last year after footage emerged of him tackling one of two gunmen who had opened fire during a Jewish event at Sydney's Bondi Beach, killing 15 people.

Ahmed wrestled a firearm from Sajid Akram and was later shot several times by a second alleged gunman, Naveed Akram.

The attack marked Australia's deadliest mass shooting in decades, and police later declared it a terrorist incident targeting the Jewish community.

A fundraiser in the days after the shooting raised more than AU$2.5m ($1.7m; £1.24m) for Ahmed, who also received a bedside visit from Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.

In a separate court matter, two of Ahmed's brothers were recently charged over allegations they threatened him and tried to extort some of the donations he had received.

Ghana News.title: Indian labourers dream of striking it rich after ‘$52,400’ diamond find
Ghana News.content:
Seven poor labourers in Panna, a diamond mining area in central India, have made a discovery that they say has the potential to change their lives forever.

The delighted men said they found a large diamond on a plot of land they had leased two years back.

On the weighing scale, the rock measured 17.96 carats and Panna diamond official Ravi Patel said it was "gem quality" - one of the finest varieties of natural diamonds that exist.

Describing the diamond as "precious", Patel said it would be put up for auction in the first half of October. He estimated its worth to be at least 5m rupees ($52,400; £38,800).

Diamond finds are not so rare in Panna, which is in Madhya Pradesh state - home to most of India's diamond reserves.

The district is among India's least developed and its residents face poverty, water scarcity and unemployment.

With few job opportunities in the city, residents hope for a prized find to improve their fortunes and the region remains a prime destination for diamond hunters.

But finders are not always keepers.

Reports say a majority of Panna's miners are daily-wage labourers who work for lease-holders - if they find a diamond, the money goes to the lease-holder and not the miners themselves.

But the latest find is one of the few cases where the actual finders would benefit.

The mine in Panna's Sarokha village was leased for a meagre sum by Akhilesh Pal and six others two years back, Press Trust of India reported.

Pal said the mine had been shut for a year and was opened only recently. On Monday, as he inspected the mine after heavy rains, he spotted the rock.

"We had been mining there for about two years," he said, "but we had no luck, so we closed the mine for a year. We had started another mine right next to it."

"When we went there to inspect the new one, we also looked inside the old mine, and that's where we found it - right on top," he added.

Patel said the diamond would be put up for sale at the next quarterly auction due in October when buyers from India and abroad would be able to bid for it.

Reports said the government would deduct a 12% royalty from the sale proceeds and the remaining money would be divided equally among the seven workers.

For some of the poor labourers, the find is set to change the course of their lives - local media reports quoted three of them as saying they were too poor to get married so far and this windfall would now help them find brides.

Ghana News.title: At least 15 die as boat sinks in Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba
Ghana News.content:
At least 15 people have died after a boat carrying dozens of people sank on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, with rescue operations continuing, officials have said.

Police said 90 passengers and five crew were onboard the vessel when it capsized on Tuesday, but it may have been overloaded, with other reports pointing to a higher number based on the registered ticket sales.

The vessel was hit by a strong wave and overturned, police added. Footage shared online appears to show the hull floating in the water.

Lake Kariba, which straddles the border with Zambia, is one of the world's largest man-made reservoirs, supporting transport and fishing and providing vital hydroelectric power to both countries.

The Zimbabwe Civil Protection Unit (CPU) said that registered ticket sales showed 114 adults were on the vessel. There could also have been an unknown number of children below ticketing age, it added.

The CPU said that 77 passengers had so far been rescued, and 15 bodies had been retrieved.

Two funeral parlours were collecting the bodies, it added.

Mutsa Murombedzi, a local member of parliament, posted a video on X of what she said was the boat at the start of the journey, adding that residents had been using it to travel across the lake to Kariba town, a journey that takes about five hours.

"We have very hard questions that require honest answers. The officials must release the correct number of people who were onboard," she wrote.

Police said more details would be released "in due course".

Ghana News.title: UK prosecutors argue Tate brothers a flight risk ahead of bail hearing
Ghana News.content:
British prosecutors are urging a US court to deny a request by influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan that they be released from jail while extradition proceedings play out, ahead of a detention hearing.

They have been held in Florida since their arrest last month after the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), which prosecutes criminal cases in England and Wales, unveiled 38 charges against them. Both have denied wrongdoing.

The CPS has said the brothers are a "flight-risk", and would attempt to interfere with the witnesses in the case, according to court filings.

The hearing on Thursday will determine whether the brothers will remain in jail for the duration of their court proceedings.

The brothers, who are dual British-US citizens, were arrested in Miami on 19 July.

They are facing a total of 59 charges, including rape and counts relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.

Both prosecutors and defence lawyers filed new documents on Monday in the Southern District of Florida federal court, ahead of the hearing on Thursday to decide whether they should be freed on bail.

While lawyers for the Tates acknowledged that bail in international extradition proceedings was unusual, they said the brothers had shown no reason to think they plan to evade criminal prosecution. The BBC has contacted the brothers' attorneys for comment.

Documents filed by the prosecution include a request from the British Embassy in Washington, and sent to the US Department of State, to deny bail.

Supporting documentation from the CPS was also filed highlighting alleged risks if the Tates are released on bond.

"Both Andrew and Tristan Tate have significant resources available to them, both in terms of money and in social media networks," prosecutors argued.

"All of the complainants in this case are vulnerable and in fear of Andrew and Tristan Tate because of the violence used towards them – several of the complainants describe being assaulted and threatened with weapons – and because of the resources available to Andrew and Tristan Tate, and because of their propensity to intimidate vulnerable complainants."

Prosecutors also cited social media posts made by Andrew Tate, in which he allegedly mocked prosecutors and suggested he could hide his identity to avoid arrest.

The new charges relate to four new accusers with allegations spanning from 2010-17, according to British prosecutors.

The brothers were already charged in 2025 with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012-15.

Police in Bedfordshire, in south-eastern England, secured European arrest warrants in 2024 for the brothers to have them returned from Romania to face the allegations.

The two moved to Romania in 2016, and were arrested on sex charges in 2022. The case there has not moved forward, and the brothers have been able to travel to the US since travel restrictions against them in Romania were lifted in early 2025.

Self-proclaimed "misogynist" Andrew Tate first rose to fame after an appearance on the British version of reality TV show Big Brother in 2016.

The former kickboxer now boasts more than 10.8 million followers on X. He and his brother have long maintained their controversial statements were just jokes or were taken out of context.

"It is believed that Andrew and Tristan Tate would attempt to draw upon that network to provide practical assistance or financial support to escape the jurisdiction and to avoid extradition proceedings if released," prosecutors argue.

He has appeared in countless videos, flaunting a luxurious lifestyle of fast cars, private jets and yachts. Prosecutors also pointed to his extensive international travel, as evidence of his ability to avoid trial.

If found guilty, the two could face life in prison.

Although the Tates have supported President Donald Trump, the White House has said it will not intervene in the case.

The decision on whether to extradite the brothers to the UK will ultimately be up to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, after it is first considered by US courts.

Ghana News.title: NAPO urges responsible political discourse, warns against insults and personal attacks
Ghana News.content:
The 2024 New Patriotic Party (NPP) running mate, Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh, has urged Ghanaians to uphold respect and responsibility in political discourse, warning against using democratic freedoms as a justification for insults and personal attacks.

In a Facebook post on Tuesday, August 11, Dr Opoku Prempeh, popularly known as NAPO, said democracy gives citizens the right to criticise leaders, political parties and ideas, but such criticism should not undermine the dignity of those being criticised.

“Criticism and insult are not the same. Criticism identifies what is wrong and can help us think about what must improve. Insult seeks only to humiliate, provoke or silence. One strengthens public debate. The other weakens it,” he said.

NAPO expressed concern that political discussions were increasingly shifting from issues to personal attacks based on individuals’ intelligence, appearance or background.

He warned that such conduct could have a negative influence on young people who look to political leaders as examples of democratic engagement.

The former Manyhia South MP stressed that respect should not be mistaken for silence or an attempt to shield public officials from scrutiny.

“Respect has never meant silence. It has never meant that elders, leaders or public officials are beyond criticism,” he said, urging citizens to challenge opposing views without treating those who hold them as enemies.

Dr Opoku Prempeh said Ghana’s democratic culture would be strengthened when political disagreements were settled through robust debate and competing ideas rather than personal attacks.

He emphasised that freedom of expression must be accompanied by responsibility, stating: “Democracy requires freedom of expression, but it also requires responsibility of expression.”

Ghana News.title: Karpowership Ghana trains fisherfolk on fire safety, hygiene and financial management
Ghana News.content:
Karpowership Ghana has organised a capacity-building training for fishermen and fishmongers from Sekondi and Essikado, focusing on environmental safety awareness, fire prevention, hygienic fish handling and financial management.

The training, held on Tuesday, August 11, brought together key institutions, including the Ghana National Fire Service, Fisheries Commission and Fidelity Bank, to provide practical education aimed at improving safety, protecting livelihoods and strengthening the resilience of the fishing communities.

The initiative forms part of Karpowership Ghana’s commitment to supporting communities through meaningful engagement and programmes that provide practical knowledge and skills to improve livelihoods.

Speaking during the training, Sandra Amarquaye, Communications Manager at Karpowership Ghana, said the company’s commitment to the communities within which it operates goes beyond its core business.

“At Karpowership Ghana, we believe that powering communities goes beyond providing electricity. It also means empowering people with the knowledge and skills they need to build safer, stronger and more sustainable livelihoods.

"This training is part of our commitment to supporting our fisherfolk and the communities we are privileged to serve.”

Fire Safety Training and Demonstration

A key component of the programme was fire safety, with the Ghana National Fire Service educating participants on fire prevention, emergency response and the safe handling of fire incidents both at the fishing harbour and in their homes.

The session was particularly relevant following recent fire incidents at the fishing harbour in Sekondi. Participants were taken through practical fire prevention measures and the appropriate steps to take during an emergency.

The Fire Service also conducted a practical demonstration and simulation, allowing participants to observe how to respond safely and effectively to a fire emergency.

Speaking on the training, Nana Appiah Mensah, a fisherman and participant, said the fire safety component was particularly useful given the recent incident at the harbour.

“The fire safety training has been very helpful to us, especially because we recently experienced a fire at the harbour. We now have a better understanding of how to prevent fires and what to do when there is an emergency. The practical demonstration made it much easier for us to understand how to respond.”

He added, “Fire can destroy our livelihoods within a very short time, so knowing how to prevent it and respond quickly is very important. What we have learnt today is knowledge we can use both at the harbour and in our homes, and we are grateful for the opportunity.”

Fisheries Commission Promotes Hygienic Fish Handling

The Fisheries Commission also educated the fishermen and fishmongers on proper and hygienic fish-handling practices, emphasising the importance of maintaining cleanliness throughout the process, from landing and handling to storage and sale.

The session highlighted the role of proper hygiene in preserving fish quality, protecting consumers and ensuring that fisherfolk derive maximum value from their catch.

Justina Annan Obeng of the Fisheries Commission said, “Proper fish handling is critical to protecting public health, maintaining the quality of fish and ensuring that fisherfolk get the best value from their catch.

"We are pleased to support this initiative because practical education such as this can help improve hygiene and food safety practices within our fishing communities.”

She noted that continuous education and collaboration among stakeholders were important in promoting better standards within the fishing sector.

Fidelity Bank Provides Financial Education

Fidelity Bank also engaged the participants on financial literacy, providing practical guidance on saving, budgeting, managing income and making sound financial decisions.

The session was designed to help fishermen and fishmongers better manage the income generated from their businesses, plan for the future and build greater financial resilience for themselves and their families.

The training provided an opportunity for the various stakeholders to address issues that directly affect the daily lives and livelihoods of the fishing community.

Through the initiative, Karpowership Ghana continues to demonstrate its commitment to community development by supporting programmes that promote safety, environmental awareness, healthy practices and sustainable livelihoods.

The company believes that empowering communities with relevant knowledge and practical skills is an important part of creating lasting impact and strengthening the communities it serves.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
