World.title: Power cuts hit parts of Durban as cold weather strains electricity network
World.content:
Parts of Durban are facing a rotating load reduction after a circuit fault. Image: canva

Residents in parts of Kloof are facing ongoing power cuts after a fault caused one of the two incoming supply circuits at Kloof Substation to fail.

The eThekwini Municipality’s Electricity and Energy Directorate said the substation is currently operating on a single supply circuit while teams work to identify and repair the fault.

The remaining circuit is under additional pressure because of increased electricity demand caused by the cold weather.



As a result, approximately 2MW of electricity will be dropped at a time to keep the transformer operating within safe limits.

Load reduction to rotate every two hours

The municipality said the power cuts will be rotated every two hours until 22:00 tonight.

It may continue tomorrow, depending on network conditions and progress with repairs.



The affected areas are:

Chelmsfordville

Forest Hills

Kloof

Krantzkloof

Padfield Park

Residents in these areas could experience periods without electricity as the load reduction is rotated.

Repairs could take longer amid bad weather in Durban

The electricity warning comes as the municipality’s Electricity and Energy Directorate is also dealing with high call volumes at its Contact Centre due to the inclement weather.



The municipality said customers are experiencing longer-than-usual call handling times as more residents report electricity outages and faults.

Customers are therefore encouraged to use the municipality’s digital platforms to log electricity outages and faults rather than relying solely on the Contact Centre.

Once a fault has been logged, it will be queued for investigation and restoration.



Electricity teams are also assessing whether some of the load can be redistributed to other substations in the area.

At the same time, fault-finding and repair work is continuing on the damaged supply circuit.

The municipality said the load reduction is necessary to prevent the remaining transformer from being overloaded while the substation operates with only one incoming supply circuit.



Residents in the affected areas are advised to prepare for the rotating disruptions, particularly during periods of high electricity demand.

World.title: While the world watches a solar eclipse, South Africa’s buried under snow
World.content:
South Africa won't see Wednesday's total solar eclipse, but it is in the grip of a rare cold snap of its own: Image Pexels

A total solar eclipse and South Africa buried under snow. Here’s why you won’t see both.

While large parts of the world turn their eyes skyward for Wednesday’s total solar eclipse, South Africa is dealing with a very different kind of spectacle: an Orange Level 6 snow warning, cut-off communities, and one of the coldest weeks of the year.

The two events are pure coincidence, and only one of them is visible from home.



Why South Africa won’t see this eclipse

Wednesday’s total solar eclipse traces a narrow path across Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain, with a partial eclipse visible across parts of Europe, North America, and northwestern Africa.

South Africa falls outside that path entirely. If you’re hoping to catch an eclipse from home this month, the one to watch is the partial lunar eclipse on 28 August instead.

Meanwhile, back on the ground in South Africa

While roughly 980 million people worldwide get some view of Wednesday’s eclipse, South Africans have been watching a different kind of rare event: a cold front and cut-off low that triggered an Orange Level 6 disruptive snow warning across the Eastern Cape’s Emalahleni, Sakhisizwe, Senqu, Elundini and Matatiele municipalities, cutting some communities off entirely.

It’s a reminder that while the rest of the world looks up this week, Mzansi has had its hands full looking out for icy roads and warnings closer to home.

I however, will be looking forward to the partial lunar eclipse on 28 August.

Would you rather chase an eclipse or a snowfall?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi …



Is it snowing in your area? If so, please send your photos to info@thesouthafrican.com

World.title: Transfer news: Stellenbosch star to Morrocan champions
World.content:
Devin Titus celebrates scoring for Stellenbosch FC in the Nedbank Cup. Image: Devin Titus Instagram

Stellenbosch FC winger Devin Titus is set for a move to Moroccan champions Maghreb de Fes after the two clubs agreed a transfer deal.

SABC Sport, through journalist Mazola Molefe, reports that Stellenbosch FC and Maghreb de Fes have agreed a club-to-club deal for the transfer of the 26-year-old.

The move could see Titus join the Botola Pro champions, who have also secured the signing of South African striker Tshegofatso Mabasa on a free transfer.



DEVIN TITUS’ STELLENBOSCH RISE

Long before becoming one of the Betway Premiership’s established stars, Titus developed his football in Cape Town.

The Bonteheuwel-born winger spent an influential period in the youth ranks of Hellenic FC before attracting attention from scouts. That eventually led to his move to Stellenbosch FC in 2020.

Titus initially progressed through the club’s youth and reserve structures. He captained the reserve side to the 2021/22 DStv Diski Challenge title and also helped them win the Premier League Next Gen Cup in the United Kingdom.



He made his senior debut under Steve Barker in January 2021 against Black Leopards.

Titus quickly established himself in the first team. In the 2022/23 campaign, he became the first Stellenbosch FC player to feature in all 30 league matches in a single season.

His breakthrough campaign continued with the 2023 Carling Knockout Cup triumph. Titus was named Player of the Tournament as Stellenbosch lifted their first major trophy.



NEXT CHAPTER

Titus has since made more than 150 appearances for Stellenbosch FC, becoming one of the club’s most-capped players.

He has also contributed more than 45 goals and assists across competitions while developing into an important figure within the club’s leadership group.

His performances earned him South Africa U-23 recognition before he progressed to the senior national team. Titus made his Bafana Bafana debut at the 2024 COSAFA Cup.



Now, the winger appears set for a new challenge in Morocco.

A move to Maghreb de Fes would represent another major step in the career of a player who has previously spoken about his ambition to play outside South Africa.

For Stellenbosch FC, it could mark the end of an important chapter for one of the players who helped establish the club as a force in South African football.

World.title: ‘Still our brother’: All Black fans touched by Ma’a Nonu’s solo Haka
World.content:
Ma'a Nonu performs the Haka against the All Blacks. Images via screenshot

Former All Blacks legend Ma’a Nonu’s performance of the Haka against the team he once played for was a gesture of goodwill, respect, and admiration for his country and culture.

It was a very last-minute decision, the now-Sharks player has revealed.

The New Zealand team beat the Durban club 54-0 in a rainy, cold match on Tuesday, 11 August, at Kings Park Stadium.



MA’A NONU ON PERFORMING THE HAKA

Speaking to SkySports, Ma’a Nonu – who joined the Sharks earlier this month in a development role – explained the significance of his responding to the All Blacks Haka, with his own.

The 44-year-old made his debut for the ABs in 2003 and boasts 103 test caps.

He said: “It was great to see the boys. To play against them for the first time was such a privilege and honour. To do the Haka and show my respect on behalf of my family to the boys and the team I love them and I will always love”.



“It was a spur-of-the-moment thing. I had questions about it the night before.

“I spoke to Tana and Tamati [Umaga] and Tamati [Ellison] and asked them for permission in terms of doing it out of respect on behalf of our team and my family.

“I thought it was the right thing to do to answer the boys and the All Blacks”.



@skysportnz A familiar face on the other side 👀🏉 Justin Marshall caught up with Ma'a Nonu after the All Blacks' clash with the Sharks. ♬ original sound – skysportnz

ALL BLACKS FANS ARE MOVED TO TEARS

On social media, All Blacks fans have shared their emotional response to Ma’a Nonu’s unexpected performance of the Haka.

Many revealed that they watched the now 42-year-old represent play for the country, and were privileged to watch him play against it, with love and respect.



“What he gave was ultimate respect and recognition”, commented one fan under an All Blacks social media post.

Others responded:

“As an AB fan, New Zealand patriot and Maori, I think this is awesome!”



“Once an All Black, always an All Black. He’s still our brother”

“You didn’t need permission to do the Haka. You will always belong to us”.



WHAT IS THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE ALL BLACKS’ HAKA?

Wearing a Sharks jersey, Ma’a Nonu performed a solo version of the Haka -the Kapa o Pango version in response to the All Blacks’ Ka Mate.

According to fans, this was not merely him indicating that the Sharks were accepting the All Blacks’ challenge, but his declaration that he was and is a proud All Black.

The Haka dates back centuries as a traditional Māori ceremonial performance used on occasions to welcome guests, celebrate achievements, mourn loved ones, and show strength and unity.



It was first performed by the All Blacks during their historic 1905 British tour.

The Kapa o Panga version was developed specifically for the national team, signifying their “pride, unity, and purpose.”

World.title: What time is kick off for the Bulls v All Blacks on Saturday?
World.content:
The All Blacks sent out a warning to the Springboks as a strong side hammered the Sharks 54-0 on Tuesday, and they will next be in action when this Saturday’s clash against the Bulls kicks off at Loftus.

It will be hoped that URC finalists, the Bulls, can put up a far sterner test after Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour has got off to a rather lacklustre start.

This Saturday’s clash at Loftus will kick off at 19:00, and a week later the Springboks and All Backs will then go head to head in the first Test at Ellis Park.



All Blacks send out a warning ahead of kick off against the Bulls

After Tuesday’s impressive win that showcased the All Blacks’ high-tempo offloading game, coach coach Dave Rennie has said there is a lot more to come.

“The (wet weather) conditions (in Durban) made it challenging, but I thought overall we did a pretty good job there, on the back of a solid defensive effort.

“Look, we’ve got a lot more in us, and we can’t afford to start games like we have in the last two here, so that’ll be a focus for us. But a really positive last 40.



“We’ve got a lot more players who have had good game time,” Rennie added. “There’s good competition for spots, and that’s really important heading into the (Joburg) Test.”

Meanwhile, Bulls coach Johan Ackermann has worryingly suggested this weekend’s battle against New Zealand is hardly ideal.

“We had to cut the break short. We have to give the guys a five-week break, but we could only give them three weeks.



“Conditioning is one thing, but your body, after three or four weeks, loses its contact ability. So we had to fast-track all of that.

“If this game wasn’t there, we would probably have been in a conditioning phase only. So it has put a bit of pressure on us.

“It’s a great occasion, but we will definitely be a bit underprepared from where we want to be. We’re building up to the URC and that’s still a few weeks away, so we don’t want to peak now,” he added.



“It’s not to use it as an excuse, but the fact that we went to the final meant we had less time to prepare than the other franchises.

“We just want to embrace the occasion and hopefully get a reward for what we’ve tried to practise over the last few weeks.”

World.title: Malawi ends South Africa repatriation drive: How many citizens returned home?
World.content:
Malawi has ended its government-assisted repatriation programme for citizens returning from South Africa, bringing to a close a costly operation launched amid growing concerns over the safety of Malawians living in the neighbouring country.

The final buses are scheduled to leave from the Malawi Consulate in Johannesburg and the Malawi High Commission in Pretoria at noon on Wednesday.

The programme was launched in June after rising tensions and violence against foreign nationals in parts of South Africa prompted thousands of Malawians to seek a return home.



But just how many Malawians have been brought back to the country through the repatriation exercise?

Malawi’s repatriation programme comes to an end

According to the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA), the final group of returnees will be processed before the Mwanza Stadium reception centre is decommissioned.

As reported by Malawi24, from Wednesday, Malawians who want to return home from South Africa will have to make their own travel arrangements.

The Malawian government will, however, continue offering routine consular assistance to its citizens in South Africa.

This includes emergency travel documents, with the government waiving the fees for Malawians returning home for a transitional period.

How many Malawians returned from South Africa?

The government-assisted programme brought home 56 723 Malawians from South Africa.



The figure includes 38 866 men and 17 857 women.

Among those who returned were 3 988 children under the age of five and 694 pregnant women, according to DoDMA.

The department also recorded seven deaths during the repatriation exercise.

The scale of the operation makes it one of Malawi’s largest organised efforts to bring citizens home from South Africa amid concerns over insecurity.

Why did Malawians return?

The repatriation programme followed rising anti-immigrant tensions and violence against foreign nationals in parts of South Africa.

Malawians were among citizens from several African countries who sought to leave the country during the unrest.

The government responded by arranging transport for citizens who wanted to return voluntarily.

The programme provided an organised route home for vulnerable people who may otherwise have struggled to make the journey themselves.

How much did Malawi spend on repatriation?

The government has not disclosed the final cost of the repatriation exercise.

However, reports indicate that more than K12 billion (about R112 million) was spent on bringing Malawians home.

The expenditure has already prompted calls for greater transparency.

Social commentator Lucky Mbewe praised the government for helping vulnerable citizens but urged authorities to provide a detailed breakdown of how the money was used.

“I would like to ask the government to make a detailed presentation of the money that was used so that taxpayers are not left in the dark,” Mbewe said.

What happens to Malawians still in South Africa?

The end of the repatriation programme does not mean Malawians in South Africa can no longer receive assistance from their government.

Officials will continue providing consular services, including emergency travel documentation.

However, citizens who now decide to return home will have to organise their own transport.

Mbewe has also urged Malawians who have returned not to rush back to South Africa, arguing that the security situation remains uncertain.

The closure of the repatriation programme therefore marks a shift from government-organised transport to normal travel arrangements, while questions remain over whether the conditions that triggered the mass return have fully improved.

World.title: Kristin Cavallari spotted soaking up the Mediterranean with her closest friends (Pics)

World.title: MTN flags lower earnings as Iran investment takes hit
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - MTN expects its reported profits to fall in the first half of the year.

This is mainly because the value of its investment in Irancell has fallen.

The telco expects headline earnings per share for the six months to June to be flat to 10 percent lower.

Earnings per share could fall by as much as 30 percent.

MTN says the main reason is that it has had to reduce the value of its investment in Iran, due to the conflict.

But it says this does not reflect the performance of its core operations.

Business in Nigeria, Ghana and Uganda continues to grow, with higher profits and strong cash generation.

MTN says cash flowing back to the parent company also remained strong.

The group says regulatory approval is now the only hurdle to its planned acquisition of IHS Towers.

MTN will release its full interim results on 24 August.

World.title: 'They go out to kill' | IPID official makes explosive KZN police task-team claims
World.content:
PRETORIA - “They go out to kill.”

That was the testimony of Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) official Len Barnabas John, who told the Madlanga Commission that rogue SAPS task teams operating in KwaZulu-Natal are using lethal force to eliminate suspects.

John is testifying before the commission on Wednesday as its focus shifts to allegations of SAPS “hit squads” operating in the province.

Some members of the KwaZulu-Natal SAPS are accused of carrying out extrajudicial killings under the guise of task-team operations.

It is alleged that officers targeted cash-in-transit robbery suspects, taxi operators and members of drug syndicates.

According to John, between 1 April 2023 and 31 May 2026, IPID investigated more than 300 cases, 77 of which involved the deaths of 149 people during police operations by task teams.

“In these 77 cases, the shootings were committed by members of the task teams,” John said, adding that the 77 deceased had no cases linking them to crimes.

Detailing IPID’s investigations, John said that in the majority of cases in which police killed suspects, fewer firearms were recovered than the number of people killed.

John said: “Their explanation all the time is that the deceased shot first at them before they could shoot, but we have identified cases which contradict the version of the police.”

He said the operations were frequently planned to take place between 11pm and 3am, when there would be fewer witnesses to observe possible wrongdoing by SAPS members.



“In the majority of our cases, there are fewer firearms found compared to the number of deceased who were at the scene. If three firearms are found and there were nine suspects, it means that six of them were unarmed.”

John said there are currently cases before the Director of Public Prosecutions in which IPID can use crime-scene reconstruction to demonstrate that the deceased did not shoot at police first.

“We have identified a few cases which contradict the version of the police. In the majority of shootings by task teams, they don’t have proper cases. In some cases, they cannot even give you the names of the deceased. They are not doing a proper investigation to arrest the suspects. They go out to kill.”

World.title: UK 'joke' candidate Binface pushes serious point about politics
World.content:
LONDON - British politics has a long-cherished reputation for attracting the weird and wonderful.

But in a pantheon of colourful characters, Count Binface, a man wearing a rubbish bin over his head, is stealing the show.

The self-described "intergalactic space warrior" from the fictional planet Sigma IX takes on hardline anti-immigrant politician Nigel Farage on Thursday in the Clacton by-election, triggered when the Reform UK leader resigned in a shock move.

With Farage running again for his seat, none of the UK's mainstream political parties is fielding candidates, having dismissed the move as a stunt designed to stall a parliamentary inquiry into his finances.

That has left the door open to Count Binface, and a host of other independent and parody candidates.

While polls give Farage a clear victory with more than 70 percent of the vote, Binface, the alter ego of comedian and comedy writer Jon Harvey, is grabbing all the attention and could win as much as 20 percent.

During almost a decade as the joke candidate in UK politics, Binface has fully embraced the absurd.

He arrives at election counts wearing a metallic dustbin-shaped helmet, a silver cape and silver-and-black armour and brandishing his razor-sharp, deadpan sense of humour.

His manifestos mix smart political satire with comedic promises to cap croissant prices, improve WiFi on UK trains and conscript people using speakerphones on public transport.

"In the UK anybody, literally anybody, is free to stand in an election, no matter how idiotic the get-up", he told AFP ahead of the 2024 London mayoral elections.

The British political system "fosters the eccentricity, the wonderment and the humour of politics", he added.

World.title: Defending champion Shelton rolls into Montreal semis
World.content:
MONTREAL - Ben Shelton took another step toward defending his ATP Montreal Masters title on Tuesday with a 6-3, 6-1 quarter-final hammering of Jakub Mensik for his 10th straight victory in Canada.

World number 10 Shelton, the last top-10 player in the field, was never challenged by the Czech in advancing to a Wednesday semi-final against fellow American Learner Tien, who ousted Spain's Daniel Merida 6-3, 6-2 in 72 minutes.

"It was a great performance for me, super happy with that and to be in the semis again," Shelton said.

Spanish teen Rafael Jodar booked a semi-final spot in only his fifth ATP Masters 1000 event by holding off France's Arthur Fils 7-6 (7/5), 6-3.

The 19-year-old will face the oldest remaining player when he plays 25-year-old American Brandon Nakashima in a Wednesday battle for a place in Thursday's final.

Nakashima reached his breakthrough Masters semi in 77 minutes as he imposed his game on Luciano Darderi 6-2, 6-3, setting up three match points with his 11th ace as the Italian missed on a drop shot.

It's the first time since 1992 that three American men have reached the last four in Canada.

Shelton was on fire in his 72-minute thrashing of Mensik, the American producing 18 winners and only three unforced errors.

Shelton has yet to lose a set at this event.

"I felt great, I played well form the ground from point one," Shelton said. "I'm right where I want to be. I maintained a high level throughout the match. I hope to continue to build on this in the semis."

Jodar shrugged off a slight tweak of his ankle in the second set against Fils and remained calm throughout as his French opponent smashed a racquet after being broken early in the second set.

Jodar, who does not turn 20 until after the US Open, has won 34 matches this season and risen to 15th in the world rankings, but sees improving his game as more important than his ranking.

"That shouldn't be your primary thing and your goal," he said. "My goal is to have fun on court and to enjoy all the tournaments that are new for me."

Fils, back after injury, saved three match points in the final game before Jodar lanced a winner to the empty court after an hour and three-quarters.

"I played a very high level today against a tough player like Arthur," Jodar said. "I had to give my best to win this match."

Nakashima, who won his fifth quarter-final of the season, credited his serve with the win.

"My serve was super important. It got me out of some tough holes," Nakashima said.

"I also took my opportunities on return when I needed to. I knew I had to open up the court. He was hitting his spots really well."

Nakashima, into his 16th career semi-final, put his confidence "at an all-time high" after his seventh victory in eight matches following a Washington semi-final run.

World.title: Farming sector keeps 900,000+ jobs despite quarterly decline
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s farming sector continues to support a strong level of employment, despite a decline in jobs during the second quarter.

Stats SA says the sector employed more than 900,000 people in the three months to June.

That is down by about 2 percent from the previous quarter, but up by more than 4 percent compared with the same period last year.

The improvement over the past year reflects stronger activity in labour intensive crops, including fruits, vegetables and field crops.

While some farmers are reporting difficulties finding workers amid the ongoing immigration debate, industry surveys suggest these shortages remain isolated rather than widespread.

However, the sector faces more risks.

Higher fuel and fertiliser costs, rising electricity prices and the threat of an El Niño-driven drought could put pressure on farmers and employment conditions in the year ahead.

World.title: DA calls for TVET staff qualifications audit
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Democratic Alliance is calling for an urgent audit of staff qualifications and leadership at Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges.

This follows oversight visits that raised concerns about lecturers teaching subjects outside their areas of expertise.

The party says the audit is needed to establish whether TVET colleges have the capacity to properly prepare young people for the job market.

DA MP Karabo Khakhau says training and education should provide a direct link between young people and their participation in the economy.

She says the current situation is therefore deeply concerning.

Khakhau points to Flavius Mareka TVET College in the Free State as an example, where lecturers specialising in mathematics have allegedly been moved to teach engineering-related subjects because the college does not have enough suitably qualified lecturers.

She says this has resulted in an imbalance in skills, with some areas having an oversupply of expertise while others lack the necessary capacity.

The DA also raised concerns about leadership at TVET colleges and accused the Department of Higher Education of failing to adequately hold institutional leaders accountable.

The party has therefore called for an audit of all staff, including lecturers, their qualifications and areas of expertise.

Khakhau says the DA has requested feedback from TVET colleges, including Gert Sibande and King Hintsa TVET colleges, within 30 days.

The audit, she says, should help determine just how widespread the problem is and whether the institutions are adequately equipped to prepare students for the workplace.

World.title: Trump's secret plane swap triggers questions and confusion
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Donald Trump confirmed that he secretly switched planes because of a threat to his life, after the Washington Post revealed the US president was smuggled out of Air Force One to a different aircraft on a catering truck.

"They wanted me to go in a different flight, a different plane -- equal safety, but they wanted me to do it, so I do it. I do what they say," Trump told reporters during a gaggle.

"I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it."

The newspaper reported Monday that the secret operation reportedly smuggled Trump off Air Force One before the plane departed, still carrying journalists and top aides who remained at apparent risk of an Iranian strike.

Trump covertly exited the presidential plane while it was on the ground in Turkey on July 8.

Some travelling media expressed anger at having unwittingly served as decoys, while others complained about deception and lack of communication from the White House.

Trump boarded the presidential jet in full view of video cameras and photographers, with AFP pictures showing two supply containers at the front and rear of the aircraft.

But he then reportedly left the plane, stepping inside one of the cargo containers, to board a smaller US Air Force aircraft positioned nearby.

"I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk," Trump told reporters. "Because that would be the plane I think that -- that they would be more likely to go for."

About a dozen journalists travelling in a separate section of Air Force One with no access to the president were unaware of the switch and flew out of Turkey on the plane despite the apparent threat from Iran, which is at war with the United States.

"Any consequential president has a lot of threats," Trump said, brushing off concerns.

"I don't worry about anything, to be honest. Whatever it is, you know my attitude: 'Whatever.'"

- Shoulder-to-air missile threat? -

The Wall Street Journal reported Israel had briefed the US about a possible shoulder-to-air missile strike on Air Force One, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was among senior officials and staff who remained on the plane.

Dispatches sent by pool media on board noted a Secret Service order that window shades be lowered during takeoff -- an unusual instruction outside of combat zones.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer on Tuesday called for Congress to be briefed "on the Iranian threats against the president, the extraordinary measures taken to get him out of Turkey."

Trump's trip to the NATO summit had already raised eyebrows after he arrived on a luxury Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar and retrofitted to carry the US president.

But it was reportedly not fitted with anti-missile security systems and the old Air Force One was called into action.

Trump claimed at the time that the new plane was being sent ahead for US troops in Britain to tour, as a treat.

At a stopover in Britain, he returned to the Qatar-gifted plane for the flight to Washington.

Asked at the time why journalists had been asked to lower window blinds he said "because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with."

"If I go, you go. Right?" Trump told reporters.

In 2000, Bill Clinton switched presidential planes at the last minute while travelling from India to Pakistan, using a decoy aircraft carrying Secret Service agents.

Joe Biden's 2023 visit to Ukraine was also shrouded in strict secrecy during a long journey by plane and train, though he was accompanied by a reporter and photographer.

World.title: You have failed Kenyans, Gachagua tells Ruto
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua when he read out President Ruto’s four-year score card during a media briefing at the party’s offices in Nairobi on August 11, 2026. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused President William Ruto of failing Kenyans and abandoning his campaign promises.

Gachagua who was speaking at the DCP headquarters accused the president of eroding democratic gains of multipartyism and swallowing opposition parties.

“Four years later, Mr. William Ruto has betrayed the trust bestowed on him by the people of Kenya, betrayed the fruits and foundation of our Nation that have been built by previous administrations under the various development blue prints such as Vision 2030,” he said.

Gachagua was addressing the press on the score card of the Kenya Kwanza administration for the four years it has been in leadership.

According to the opposition figure, President Ruto had promised to uphold the rule of law, build a secure, just and democratic Kenyan founded on the constitution but he had abandoned all of the promises.

He added that there were promises of professionalising the National Police Service, safeguarding human rights, protecting Kenyans and strengthening the administration of justice while ensuring security agencies are accountable to the constitution.

Gachagua alleged that the Kenya Kwanza administration had allowed goonism and drug abuse to thrive adding that the country had also become a bedrock of extrajudicial killings and an abductors playground.

He said that during campaigns they had promised to amend and operationalise the National Coroners Service Act of 2017 to establish the Coroner General’s office to remove the burden of probing deaths from the regular police channels and Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

Gachagua said that proposed amendments were aimed at removing potential conflict of interest and ensuring transparency in handling unexplained deaths, enforced disappearances or fatalities caused by the police.

“Four years later, this promise has not been fulfilled.”

He accused the government of overseeing the arrest and rendition of government critics from Turkey, Uganda, Tanzania and South Sudan adding that officials attached to a construction company from China were deported when they protested the awarding of a contract to rivals.

“Kenyans are not safe, our children are not safe, investors are not safe and foreigners are not safe. Foreigners are not safe, Investors are not safe, no one in Kenya is safe.”

He accused the President of limiting the freedom of the press through sponsored disinformation campaigns and also citing the attempted abduction of Standard Group’s Associated Editor Alex Kiprotich in Nakuru on June 26, 2026.

According to Gachagua the government had failed to fight corruption despite promising to do so adding that it had entrenched graft as a way of life in Kenya.

World.title: Wamboka: Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang'i should back Sifuna
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kabuchai Mp Majimbo kalasinga and his counterpart Jack Wamboka during a press briefing on Monday. [Juliet Omelo, Standard]

The political battle for the 2027 presidency has intensified, with leaders allied to the Linda Mwananchi movement urging opposition figures Kalonzo Musyoka, Rigathi Gachagua and Fred Matiang’i to abandon their presidential ambitions and back Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

Bumula MP Jack Wamboka made the call after a three-day political tour of Western Kenya by the Linda mwananchi brigade, saying the region had demonstrated growing grassroots support for Sifuna.

Wamboka said the tour was a major success, with close to 22 rallies held in three days. He added that the crowds reflected growing enthusiasm for Sifuna, particularly among young people, women, political aspirants and ordinary voters.

“We respect you, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i. We know you have what it takes but in 2027, we ask you to stand with Sifuna,” Wamboka said.

He said the reception in Western Kenya showed that Sifuna’s campaign was gaining national attention.

The first time MP said Sifuna had focused on issues affecting Western Kenya, particularly the collapse of industries and the struggling sugar sector. He pointed to Mumias and Nzoia sugar factories, saying their decline had left farmers and workers suffering.

Wamboka accused National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula of failing to deliver development promises made to Bungoma residents citing unfinished roads and the stalled Bungoma stadium, saying several projects lacked adequate funding despite repeated commitments to voters during the campaigns.

He also questioned Wetang’ula’s political record, citing past controversies and accusing the Speaker of failing to live up to his promises adding that voters should judge leaders by what they deliver, not by speeches alone.

Kabuchai MP Majimbo Kalasinga said the tour had proved that Sifuna’s bid was gaining grassroots support.

“Edwin Sifuna is going for president, nothing else,” he said.

He said supporters contributed small amounts to the campaign, arguing that the movement was being funded by ordinary Kenyans rather than wealthy political backers. He said crowds turned up voluntarily.

Kalasinga also announced that Linda Mwananchi would hold a rally in Homa Bay on August 16 despite local warnings. He said Sifuna had a right to campaign anywhere in Kenya.

He called for peaceful competition and warned against attempts to block the rally or restrict political activity in the region emphasising that Kenya is for everyone, constitutionally, peacefully and equally.

They two vowed to fight for the Linda Mwananchi name.

The Wamboka-Kalasinga push adds momentum to Sifuna’s campaign and pressures opposition leaders to unite before the 2027 election.

World.title: Kindiki defends government's development agenda in Mt Kenya
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki and Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on August 10, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reiterated the government’s commitment to ensure equitable development.

Prof Kindiki said that President William Ruto’s government has initiated many development projects in Mt Kenya to transform livelihoods.

“Am advising the people against being deceived to leave the government to join the opposition where nothing is being provided,” he said.

The Deputy President said the road projects which had stalled have since been revived after the government released Sh176 billion owed to contractors to ensure completion of 6,000km.

He spoke at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on Sunday, where he was the chief guest during celebrations to mark 100 years since the establishment of Gaichanjiru Mission Hospital managed by the Catholic Diocese of Murang'a.

Kindiki, who was accompanied by Cabinet Secretaries Alice Wahome (Lands) and Rebecca Miano (Tourism), said that the government has impacted the region with affordable houses estimated at 180,000 units, modern markets and student hostels that have created employment for hundreds of skilled and unskilled persons.

He said the church has a history of partnering with the government in matters concerning development and empowerment of the less fortunate in the community.

“In Murang’a the government has ensured all the projects that KeRRA under Eng Antony Mwaura was working on are completed to give the locals value for money,” said the DP.

During the event, the President gave Sh10 million for procurement of equipment for the health facility, where more than Sh20 million was raised.

Ruto also gave Sh 50 million and directed the Housing Department to facilitate construction of the hospital's ICU, HDU, theatre and laboratory

Kindiki lauded efforts by Wahome that have seen Murang’a County benefit from Sh27 billion programmes from her ministry.

“Murang’a through her efforts has 27 modern markets, Affordable Housing Programme units, and student hostels, programmes that have engaged hundreds of persons,” he said.

World.title: Charlene Ruto's Koito lights up Kilgoris
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Ruto, is engaged to Tanzanian entrepreneur Isaiah Yunge.

The drums rolled, traditional songs filled the air and dancers swayed in colourful rhythm as Kilgoris was transformed into a spectacular theatre of love, culture, wealth and political power.

At the expansive Intonna Heritage Farm in Naserian Village, President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Chelagat Ruto, took a major traditional step towards marriage as the First Family hosted her Koito ak Chaik—a colourful Kalenjin engagement and farewell ceremony.

For hours, the skies above Kilgoris were punctuated by helicopters ferrying distinguished guests to the President’s family property, while luxury vehicles streamed through the gates carrying politicians, government officials, business personalities, relatives and friends.

On the ground, the mood was unmistakably festive. Traditional songs echoed across the expansive farm as dancers moved to the rhythm, colourful attire transformed the venue into a sea of elegance and culture, and guests embraced the joy of a ceremony that combined an ancient African tradition with the unmistakable grandeur of Kenya’s First Family.

It was romance wrapped in tradition—and tradition presented on a spectacular scale.

The guest list read almost like a roll call of Kenya’s political establishment. Leaving the Narok delegation was Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who joined Kilgoris MP Julius Sunkuli and former Narok Governor Samuel Tunai in celebrating the First Family on the special occasion.

The ceremony also brought together elected leaders from across Narok County, creating an impressive gathering of the county’s political establishment at the heart of Trans Mara.

From governors and Senators to MPs, the event brought together leaders from across the country. Top government officials and senior executives too came dressed for the ceremony

The fashion became part of the spectacle. Brown, maroon and other earthy tones dominated the scene, blending effortlessly with the traditional African setting. It was a celebration in which political leaders seemed determined to make an entrance as memorable as the occasion itself.

But beyond the political faces and the luxury was the heartbeat of the ceremony—culture. Traditional songs rang across the farm. Dancers moved with energy and precision, their performances adding colour and rhythm to a celebration centred on family and love.

The atmosphere shifted between moments of emotion and bursts of exuberance as relatives, friends and guests celebrated Charlene’s transition into a new stage of life.

The contrast was striking. Modern wealth arrived by helicopter, while ancient traditions were celebrated through song and dance. Luxury vehicles lined up outside as cultural performers entertained guests inside. Political heavyweights mingled with family elders.

Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

And amid the glamour, the central message remained simple: Charlene and her fiancé, Isaiah Yunge, had brought together not just two families but two countries.

Yunge is a Tanzanian technology entrepreneur and digital innovation enthusiast associated with Goodsam Technologies and is a co-founder of Smart Kaya LLC, a smart-home technology venture.

He has been recognised among Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 and received the Queen’s Young Leaders Award in 2018. His interest in technology reportedly began at an early age. At 17, he was selected as a UNICEF Africa Youth Ambassador and participated in international advocacy around children's rights.

He later pursued training in sustainable business models through the Swedish Institute, studied Leading Change at Cambridge University and became an alumnus of the Harvard Ministerial Leadership Program.

For all its glamour, the heart of the celebration remained the centuries-old tradition of Koito. Among the Kalenjin, it is a significant engagement ceremony through which the families of the bride and groom formally meet, bless the relationship, exchange gifts and discuss dowry arrangements.

It is a moment when families begin the process of becoming one. The Chaik aspect gives the occasion an emotional dimension, symbolising the farewell of a daughter as she prepares to leave her parental home and begin a new chapter with her husband. Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

For Charlene, the symbolism was profound. Surrounded by her parents, family, friends and some of the country’s most powerful political figures, she was celebrated not simply as the President’s daughter, but as a daughter taking a traditional step towards marriage.

The songs, dances and blessings gave the occasion an emotional warmth that stood in contrast to the scale of the event.

Yet there was no escaping the extraordinary display of wealth surrounding the celebration. Helicopters arriving overhead. Luxury vehicles streaming through the gates. High-ranking government officials and elected leaders arriving in motorcades. Elegant outfits and carefully coordinated colours.

It was a spectacle that demonstrated the resources, networks and influence available to one of Kenya’s most powerful families. The ceremony was therefore more than a social event.

For Charlene, however, beyond the helicopters, politicians, fashion and cameras was the quiet meaning of the day.

A daughter was being prepared to leave one home and begin another. Two families were being brought together.

Love was at the centre. Culture provided the rhythm. Wealth supplied the grandeur. And political power provided the spectacle.

For one unforgettable Saturday, Charlene Ruto’s Koito turned Kilgoris into a glittering stage where romance, tradition, influence and prosperity met under the Narok sky.

World.title: Police join protest victims' Sh25.75m reparations payout
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prof. Makau Mutua, Chairperson of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations. [File,Standard]

A protest reparations panel has approved compensation for 49 police officers, awarding them Sh25.75 million alongside payments to civilians who suffered human rights violations.

The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations approved seven claims involving severe injuries, 37 for moderate injuries and five for minor injuries, according to an update issued Friday, August 7.

"In acknowledgement of the dedication by our uniformed officers to protecting the public, the Panel has resolved to grant appropriate compensation for the human rights violations they sustained during the period in question," the panel said.

The inclusion of police officers adds a new dimension to a compensation programme created against the backdrop of protests in which police conduct has faced scrutiny.

During protests between June 17 and July 7, 2025, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) recorded 65 deaths, 342 civilian injuries and 171 injuries to police officers.

IPOA said most of the deaths were linked mainly to police actions during crowd-control operations.

The compensation programme grew out of the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO) process, which sought to address political and governance tensions in Kenya.

The government later set aside Sh2 billion for victims of human rights violations linked to protests and other demonstrations between 2017 and 2025.

The panel reported that it has processed 680 claims and disbursed Sh896.1 million in compensation.

The panel listed three phases of payments as Sh448.7 million in the initial phase, Sh225.4 million in the second phase and Sh247.95 million in the third phase.

The latest phase covered 175 civilian victims and included 50 fatalities, 46 severe injuries, 49 moderate injuries, 21 minor injuries and nine economic-loss claims.

The panel reported total payments of Sh222 million for the phase.

However, 472 claims submitted through IPOA and KNCHR remain outstanding because applicants have not provided enough supporting documents.

The panel is working with IPOA regional offices to locate affected victims and their beneficiaries and obtain the documents required to process the claims.

The backlog includes 594 of the 600 economic-loss claims received by the panel. Only four have been processed and compensated.

The panel has also received nine claims under the sexual offences category. Eight have been processed and compensated while one remains pending.

Claims involving enforced disappearances remain under review because the panel says the cases require investigation and verification before they can be approved, referred for further investigation or declared ineligible.

The panel has also reclassified three claims from minor to severe after reviewing medical reports and additional submissions.

It approved above-scale compensation for five victims whose injuries it described as permanent and life-altering and said it would recommend that President Ruto include them in a government-funded lifetime medical scheme.

World.title: EACC arrests Kitui County Chief Officer over Sh17.48m procurement fraud
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors arrested by EACC. [Joh Muia, Standard]

The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has arrested Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors over alleged conflict of interest and procurement irregularities involving Sh17.48 million contracts.

In a statement on Thursday, EACC CEO Abdi Mohamud said investigations found that Kivoto, who served in the Departments of Agriculture & Fisheries and Irrigation, allegedly traded with the county through five proxy companies: Shanel Construction Ltd, ECO Stone Ltd, AZ Links Ltd, DTK Construction Ltd, and 4-Walls Ltd.

The companies were paid a total of Sh14.1 million by the county between the 2018/2019 and 2024/2025 financial years.

EACC further established that three of the directors, Josephine Mwikali Wambua of Shanel Construction, Makoma Wambua of AZ Links and Emmanuel Wambua of ECO Stone are relatives of Kivoto. There were also financial transactions between Kivoto and directors of DTK Construction and 4-Walls.

Following investigations, the file was forwarded to the DPP, who approved charges against nine suspects, including conflict of interest, abuse of office, money laundering, and corrupt procurement.

Those arrested are Gladys Mami Kivoto, Josephine Mwikali Wambua Director, Shanel Construction, Roselyne Kyambi Kilonzi Director, Shanel Construction, Mary Mueni Mbiti Director, DTK Construction & 4-Walls, Jonathan Kivondo Kieti Director, DTK Construction and Onesmus Munyao Nzioka Director, ECO Stone.

EACC directed Makoma Wambua of ECO Stone, Emmanuel Wambua of AZ Links, and Stella Nthenya Kioko of AZ Links who are reportedly in hiding to present themselves at the EACC Lower Eastern Regional Office in Machakos or the nearest EACC office for processing.

The suspects are expected to be arraigned at the Kitui Law Courts.

World.title: High Court orders striking nurses back to work
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Uasin Gishu County nurses strike over delayed payments and unfulfilled Collective Bargaining Agreement [Wycliff Kipsang, Standard]

Nurses across the 47 counties have been ordered to report back to work immediately or face legal action from the counties.

Justice Monica Mbaru of the Employment and Labour Court in Mombasa issued orders temporarily stopping the nationwide nurse strike that commenced on July 29, 2026, and ordered the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives (KNUNM) to direct its members back to work.

Justice Mbaru said on Wednesday that any nurse absent from work without proper and lawful cause shall face disciplinary action.

This is after Mombasa County Government and its Public Service Board successfully enjoined the 46 county governments to make the order national.

“In the interim, the KNUNM (respondent) is hereby restrained from undertaking any industrial action relating to the strike notices dated July 21 and July 29 and shall direct all its members to resume duty forthwith and unconditionally to allow the court to address the claim herein on a priority basis,” said Justice Mbaru.

The judge ordered all county labour officers in the 47 counties to record attendance of nurses who report to work and compile a report in court on September 22, 2026.

“Any member of the KNUNM who will be noted by the County Labour Officer as absent from duty without lawful cause shall allow the counties to issue necessary notice to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken,” said Justice Mbaru.

In their petition certified urgent, Mombasa County claimed that the nurses strike has crippled services in public hospitals across all the 47 counties, thereby placing patients facing emergency and inpatient care at risk.

In Mombasa County, the nurses strike paralysed medical services at all medical facilities, including Coast General Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital, Likoni District Hospital and Shimo La Tewa GK Prison Hospital.

Mombasa County, through its Counsel Murtaza Tajbhai, said that the strike had turned from a labour disagreement to a matter of immense public interest.

Tajbhai said that the nurses’ union proceeded with the said strike despite the Mombasa Public Service Board inviting the KNUNM officials for talks to avert the said strike.

The union had raised concerns over the 2025-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), implementation of the 2017 Return to Work Formula and pension terms for Universal Health Coverage staff care guidelines for nurses and the reinstatement of 46 nurses dismissed in Kisii County.

However, in their petition, Mombasa County said that the said grievances could not be addressed by each county individually.

Mombasa County Service Board Chief Executive Officer Fadhil Maamum told the court in his affidavit that most of the demands required consultation with national institutions like the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, while others cannot be implemented immediately given their significant financial implications.

He said that nurses under Mombasa County have no salary arrears and had met some of the union’s demands through negotiations.

Maamum said that while the nurses’ grievances can be resolved, the patients do not have the luxury of time.

“Nurses are designated essential service providers under the Labour Relations Act and the industrial action was unlawful because the statutory dispute resolution mechanism had not been exhausted," said Maamum.

He said the court's intervention will allow for negotiations and safeguard the constitutional right to healthcare.

However, the Union said that the strike was after failed action by the counties to meet their agreed grievances despite continued negotiations.

The nurses said they will not be reporting to work unless guided by the union.

World.title: PM inspects development and service projects in Gharbiya Governorate
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly began an inspection tour of Gharbiya Governorate on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to inaugurate and inspect a number of development, service, and government projects, accompanied by several ministers and senior officials.

During the tour, Madbouly highlighted Gharbiya’s competitive advantage as one of Egypt’s traditional industrial hubs and a major agricultural governorate. He also reviewed progress on projects implemented under the presidential “Decent Life” initiative, which aims to improve basic services and enhance the quality of life in rural communities.

The tour included healthcare facilities, family medicine centers, drinking water and wastewater projects, as well as the inauguration of a regional branch of the Consumer Protection Agency.

Gharbiya Governor Alaa Abdel Moaty said 221 projects have been completed in Zefta district, covering 55 villages and 92 hamlets and serving around 560,000 people. The projects include government and agricultural service complexes, healthcare facilities, roads, bridges, and irrigation infrastructure.

PM: Egypt Prioritizes Drinking Water Services

During the tour, Madbouly inaugurated the Nahtay water station in Zefta, stressing that the state places particular importance on the drinking water sector as a vital service directly linked to citizens’ daily lives and health.

The station was upgraded and its efficiency enhanced under the presidential “Decent Life” initiative as part of ongoing efforts to improve drinking water services and the quality of life in Egyptian villages.

Madbouly said drinking water projects implemented under the initiative are contributing to a significant improvement in basic services across targeted villages. He added that these projects aim to provide safe, high-quality drinking water and ensure reliable services for citizens.

The upgrades to the Nahtay station are expected to increase water production, improve pumping rates, and enhance the stability of services provided to residents.

Madbouly stressed the importance of accelerating the completion of “Decent Life” projects, addressing any obstacles affecting implementation, and maximizing their impact on the quality of life in targeted communities.

PM Inspects Sandbast Family Medicine Center

Madbouly also inspected the Family Medicine Center in Sandbast village, Zefta district, describing healthcare projects under the “Decent Life” initiative as a key pillar of the state’s efforts to invest in human development.

He said such projects reflect the state’s commitment to providing comprehensive and advanced healthcare services in villages, ensuring that citizens have access to quality medical care close to their homes while contributing to improved quality of life and sustainable development.

Minister of Health and Population Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the Sandbast Family Medicine Center represents a model for modern primary healthcare facilities designed to bring medical services closer to citizens and support comprehensive health coverage.

Built on an area of 2,050 square meters, the three-story center serves more than 47,000 citizens and includes specialist clinics, family medicine and family planning clinics, a dental clinic, a first-aid unit, a fully equipped pharmacy, a medical laboratory, maternal and child healthcare services, a radiology center, and a state-funded treatment clinic.

The center also provides services under Egypt’s presidential public health initiatives, including screening and treatment for chronic and kidney diseases, early detection and treatment of hearing impairment among newborns, women’s health services, maternal and fetal care, early detection of genetic diseases, healthcare for the elderly, and cancer screening and treatment.

Abdel Ghaffar said the center has spared residents the time, cost, and difficulty of traveling to Zefta General Hospital, around five kilometers away, to receive medical care.

During his inspection, Madbouly toured the center’s clinics and spoke with medical staff about working hours and services. Doctors said healthcare services are available around the clock, while the family planning clinic receives up to 900 visitors per month and provides all services free of charge.

Madbouly also spoke with residents about the quality of services provided at the center. They expressed satisfaction with the healthcare services and said the new facility had significantly reduced the need to travel for treatment, particularly for elderly people, women, and children.

Gharbia Governor Alaa Abdel Moaty said the governorate is witnessing a major transformation in healthcare infrastructure under the “Decent Life” initiative. He added that the Sandbast center represents an important addition to healthcare services in Zefta and supports preparations for the implementation of the Comprehensive Health Insurance System.

The prime minister was accompanied during the tour by the ministers of health and population, local development and environment, agriculture and land reclamation, and housing, as well as lawmakers and senior officials.

World.title: PM: LE450B allocated to “Hayah Karima” projects benefiting 20M citizens
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said the total funding allocated to completed projects under the presidential “Hayah Karima” (Decent Life) initiative nationwide has exceeded LE 450 billion.

Speaking at a press conference following the opening and inspection of a number of service and development projects in Gharbiya Governorate, Madbouly said the completed projects have been implemented in more than 1,450 villages, benefiting around 20 million citizens.

Madbouly said the progress achieved under the presidential “Hayah Karima” initiative represents the outcome of extensive efforts, describing the initiative as, “by all measures, Egypt’s project of the 21st century.”

He explained that Gharbiya Governorate is currently putting the final touches on the completion of all “Hayah Karima” projects, noting that the projects have either already been received or are at the stage of preliminary handover, paving the way for their full operation.

Madbouly said Gharbiya is among the governorates where implementation of the initiative has been fully completed, adding that the completion of Phase One in the remaining governorates will take place successively, with its completion expected to be announced over the coming weeks.

He underscored the substantial scale of funding spent on the completed “Hayah Karima” projects nationwide.

Madbouly said the projects being implemented in Egyptian villages go beyond developing individual villages, forming part of a comprehensive effort to improve services and infrastructure on a large scale.

He explained that comparing the conditions of villages before the implementation of the initiative’s projects with their current status clearly demonstrates the extent of development achieved.

As an example of the scale of development, he noted that the rate of wastewater coverage in villages across Gharbiya Governorate stood at 26 percent in 2014, while it has now risen to 77 percent following the completion of the initiative’s first phase, in addition to other projects to be added to the villages targeted under the second and third phases.

The Prime Minister pointed out that development efforts have not been limited to infrastructure projects, but have also been carried out in parallel to improve the level of services provided to citizens, particularly healthcare services through health units, medical centers and hospitals, alongside the provision of medicines and medical services.

He explained that the water treatment plants constructed under the initiative now cover projected needs through 2050.

The Prime Minister added that development efforts have also extended to bringing modern services to villages, including natural gas networks and fiber-optic telecommunications lines, stressing that the ongoing projects represent genuine development of Egyptian villages.

Madbouly explained that implementing this massive project faced numerous challenges, particularly the lack of comprehensive information at the outset regarding the services already available in villages, the complexity of implementing the projects, and challenges related to allocating land needed for their construction.

He pointed out that overcoming these challenges required tremendous efforts involving millions of Egyptians, including consulting firms, universities and construction companies, stressing that the scale of the work carried out reflects the magnitude of the project and the extensive efforts it has required over the past years.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said the government is contributing to improving the quality of life for more than 60 million citizens through the three phases of the major “Decent Life” (Haya Karima) initiative.

He said the government had gained considerable experience following the completion of the first phase of the initiative, adding that the new phase is currently focused as a top priority on sanitation projects and improving water quality, as well as healthcare projects, including hospitals and health and medical units, in addition to schools.

Madbouly said the initiative had also created significant employment opportunities, noting that the unemployment rate had fallen below 6 percent. “We are moving in the right direction despite all the unprecedented challenges we are facing,” he said.

The prime minister also highlighted the “Ras El Hekma” medical project in Matrouh, which has been fully developed, as well as expansion plans across the governorate. He pointed to the construction of an entirely new building for Alamein Hospital and the “Alam El Roum” Hospital, the governorate’s main hospital, which has hundreds of beds.

He added that major medical services are being implemented alongside housing and development projects, as well as the Alam El Roum project being developed through an Egyptian-Qatari partnership.

Madbouly stressed that tourism is a genuine source of income for Egypt, saying it is encouraging to see the large presence of foreign tourists on the North Coast. This, he noted, means an inflow of foreign currency into the country, as well as job opportunities for young people living in these areas throughout the year.

He noted that the North Coast has strong tourism potential, pointing to the acceleration in the development of tourism projects. Such projects, he said, will create job opportunities and generate billions of dollars in revenues for the state.

The prime minister also touched on the high-speed railway serving the development process, saying it would help citizens travel from Cairo to Matrouh, as well as along the “Ain Sokhna-Matrouh-Salloum” route, alongside electricity, energy and development projects.

He stressed that the government is safeguarding the state’s rights and that an integrated vision for the development of the North Coast will benefit the people of Matrouh by generating jobs and development opportunities.

Madbouly affirmed that development is at the heart of every part of Egypt, urging people to consider the scale of development achieved over the past 12 years, compared with the situation in Egypt before that period and the country’s current position, despite the unprecedented external challenges.

He added that the government is focusing on improving citizens’ quality of life and has comprehensive plans to address existing challenges. The government is nearing completion of a program aimed at launching an economic transformation over the next three years.

“Our goal is to anticipate all possible scenarios that could unfold globally and their impact on us, including the continuation of the conflicts currently taking place,” he said.

On the energy sector, Madbouly said the government reviews the file on a weekly basis with the officials responsible for it.

He added that, under the visions and strategies set by the political leadership for the sector since 2014, the state has undertaken a large number of projects whose benefits are now being realized and whose returns are being reaped during the current phase.

He affirmed that Egypt is capable of meeting the energy sector’s needs over the coming period.

World.title: Finance Minister: LE 6 bln targeted for cash payment of third tranche of exporters’ dues
World.content:
Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said the government is targeting the allocation of six billion LE to pay in cash the third tranche of overdue dues owed to exporters for shipments made before July 1, 2024.

Kouchouk said applications from exporting companies seeking to benefit from the third tranche of the cash payment initiative will be accepted from Aug. 16 through Oct. 1, with payments scheduled to be disbursed on Oct. 22.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the minister said more than LE 80 billion has been paid to exporters over the past six years, adding that the government aims to clear all outstanding dues within two years.

He noted that LE 48 billion has been allocated in the current budget to accelerate the provision of export support, while export subsidies reached LE 28 billion in fiscal year 2025/2026, marking annual growth of 55%.

Kouchouk said there is ongoing coordination and integration with the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade to develop the export system and boost the export sector.

He stressed that the government is working to provide exporters with liquidity to support the growth and competitiveness of Egypt’s goods and services exports, adding that it aims to significantly increase annual allocations for export support and promotion in order to open new markets for Egyptian products.

Meanwhile, Nevine Mansour, the minister’s adviser for economic institutions’ relations, said LE 12.6 billion in cash had been paid to around 2,500 exporting companies during the last fiscal year.

She noted that the amount represented the total value of the first and second tranches of overdue dues paid in cash during fiscal year 2025/2026, instead of being paid over two fiscal years.

World.title: Petroleum Minister: Proactive plans remain in place to secure natural gas market needs
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi has affirmed that the petroleum sector continues to implement comprehensive, proactive plans to secure the local market’s natural gas needs.

He stressed the importance of managing shifts in consumption with high efficiency and flexibility, while maintaining maximum readiness to handle any emergencies or developments.

This came as the minister reviewed the operational status of the national natural gas grid directly from the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO) control center.

He inspected the steady flow of gas to various domestic sectors and evaluated strategic plans to meet energy demands through the remainder of the summer season.

During his visit, the minister verified uninterrupted gas supplies to power generation plants to ensure grid stability amid soaring temperatures.

He also monitored deliveries to the industrial sector to guarantee that factories operate at full capacity, alongside fulfilling domestic market requirements and export commitments.

Badawi noted that decisive state measures, backed by the political leadership and the government, have successfully met local demand throughout the first half of the summer.

Key actions included procuring regasification vessels and natural gas shipments, boosting domestic production, and implementing forward-looking supply strategies, he said.

Concluding his remarks, the minister underscored the necessity of continuous coordination between the petroleum and electricity sectors, alongside other relevant authorities.

This integrated approach aims to guarantee sustainable energy supplies for all state sectors moving forward, supported by real-time monitoring of the grid, consumption rates, and supply flows.

World.title: What Trump’s catering-truck escape says about a war that won’t end
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s use of a catering truck in a secret escape from a NATO country amid an Iranian threat is the latest embarrassing twist of a war that repeatedly defies his claims of victory.

The Secret Service did its job by using whatever method was necessary to spirit Trump out of Turkey in July, ultimately on an alternative jet to one that has been bringing presidents home safely since the 1990s.

But belated revelations about the drama, first reported by the Washington Post, kicked up a major new political storm. Most significantly, the ruse conjured up damaging new imagery about an unpopular war that Trump can’t end.

The existence of a potential threat against the president doesn’t in itself mean his war against Iran is a failure. But the spectacle of him leaving incognito after a NATO summit is likely to be interpreted overseas as a new affront to American power. It also raises this question: If Trump cannot guarantee his own safety on the territory of a major ally, how can his administration’s case that it has all but obliterated Iran’s military capability and regional terror threat be fully believed?

Iran has yet to comment. But its apparent success in metaphorically forcing Trump to take cover is a propaganda coup. For all the president’s bravado, the regime doesn’t seem to be heading for collapse or begging for a deal.

The hijinks at Ankara airport are just the latest occasion when reality has mocked the administration’s rosy war narrative.

Trump on Monday, for instance, insisted yet again that the Strait of Hormuz was “open now.” Yet the critical waterway remains effectively under Iran’s control, meaning that US forces have been fighting for months to return to the status quo — and open strait — that prevailed before the war.

Everyone has meanwhile lost count of Trump’s predictions that a deal is imminent, only for the stalemate to grind on.

In another sign of apparent US strategic disarray, the war that Trump declared won after a few days has seriously depleted US missile stocks, including nearly 80 percent of interceptors for a key missile defense system, CNN reported last week.

Trump ‘hates anything like this’

President Donald Trump holds a press briefing at the White House after a man with a gun stormed the White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner in Washington, DC, on April 25. Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

Oddly, given their position, presidents often travel through scruffy locations, since security precautions force them to enter buildings through underground garages, back entrances, kitchens and service elevators. So even the kingpin of gold-plated Mar-a-Lago may not have been too shocked to slum it in a hydraulic catering truck in Ankara.

But Trump’s clandestine departure from Turkey sits poorly with the president’s self-image as a winner and a strongman.

Even when bloodied and rumpled after an 2024 assassination attempt, he rose, pumped his fist and said “fight, fight.” When a gunman tried to rush the White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner in April, Trump went on TV to insist he wouldn’t be intimidated and the show must go on.

“Donald Trump absolutely hates anything like this,” the president’s first-term communications director Alyssa Farah Griffin told CNN’s Phil Mattingly on “The Lead” Tuesday. “He hated when he had to go to the bunker because of the threat environment in the White House … He wanted to go back immediately to show he’s not scared, he’s not running.”

Griffin, now a CNN commentator, added, “This speaks to me that this was a very real threat. If he’s willing to take these measures and to do it. It speaks to the moment we’re in, in the Middle East.”

Trump’s tarmac bait-and-switch also fueled new controversy over the presidential plane fleet, since he’d previously abandoned plans to fly his new red, white, and blue jet donated by Qatar, which critics warn lacks sufficient security systems for a president. The president and the White House have denied that a threat led them to resort to a backup aircraft.

People board Air Force One at Ankara Esenboga Airport in Ankara, Turkey, on July 8. Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

Then, there’s the issue of whether staff, Secret Service agents, journalists and crew were in mortal danger when they took off on a plane that Trump had been shown on television boarding minutes previously — before secretly leaving.

On Tuesday, Trump was asked by reporters why it was considered too dangerous for him to fly on one of the planes usually used as Air Force One while the same did not apply to members of the press.

“The plane that I flew on was at greater risk … because that would be the plane, I think, that they would be more likely to go for,” the president said.

But his comment didn’t answer the question at issue, because by climbing aboard the presidential jet, he’d given every impression he planned to travel on it — before his unannounced departure.

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, told CNN’s Erin Burnett Tuesday that Trump “put people in harm’s way to save himself — that’s who Donald Trump is.”

Pritzker then tied the incident to the wider war, saying, “He’s willing to put troops in harm’s way … he slinked away literally in a catering truck while the reporters and his own staff were on a plane that apparently was under threat.”

Pritzker’s comments put the drama at the center of the midterm election battle. And there will likely be investigations if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress in November.

Trump may spend the rest of his life facing threats from Iran

An Iranian flag is waved under a billboard with graphic showing Strait of Hormuz and the sewn lips of President Donald Trump, in downtown Tehran, Iran, on May 6. Vahid Salemi/AP

Trump, who has survived at least two direct assassination attempts, is likely to spend the rest of his life under the threat of an attack from Iran. His exposure dates to his first term, when he ordered an attack that killed Iranian general Qasem Soleimani. Iran’s incentive grew when Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in US and Israeli air strikes at the start of the current war.

Choreographed displays of defiance at Khamenei’s funeral in July saw protesters demand the death of the president. So there is good reason for the Secret Service to take any intelligence about possible attacks seriously. There have been past reports of killings of Iranians opposed to the Tehran government in Turkey, and the Iranian regime has been one of the world’s most prominent exporters of terrorism.

“I do find it entirely plausible that there might be a serious threat to the president by some Iranian-backed entity. The US, the UK, a number of European states have foiled or disrupted Iranian-backed attacks over the last several years, frankly going back decades,” retired US Army Lt. Gen. Karen Gibson said on “The Lead” Tuesday. “They’ve demonstrated an intent and a capacity to do this.”

Trump warned in July that 1,000 missiles were “Locked and ⁠Loaded and aimed at the ​Islamic Republic of Iran, with ​thousands of more to immediately follow” if it attempted or succeeded in assassinating him. In practice, any response to the death of a president would not be decided by orders he left behind, but by his successor, in this case, Vice President JD Vance. A need to restore US deterrence and credibility would likely mandate a massive US escalation.

Still, it’s notable that Trump did not respond to his indecorous departure from Turkey with an emotional response of his own. Perhaps his success in keeping it quiet until now saved face. But he has also consistently reached forks in the road and balked at mission creep that could result in heavy US casualties.

It’s possible that the Secret Service’s actions in Turkey may have averted an attack that could have drawn the US deeper into a quagmire.

But Trump’s furtive flight from Turkey makes it much harder for him to argue he’s made the world safer.

World.title: Trump declines to rule out declaring a national security emergency to control the 2026 election
World.content:
President Donald Trump in a new interview declined to rule out declaring a national security emergency as a means to try to assert more control over the 2026 midterm elections.

It’s merely the latest warning sign that Trump could try to mess with the election not just by baselessly claiming voter fraud and challenging the results afterward — as he did in 2020, leading to a violent riot at the US Capitol — but by trying to unilaterally take control before votes are cast.

In the interview, Wayne Allyn Root of Real America’s Voice pitched such a scenario to Trump. He suggested it as an alternative, given the Senate has failed to pass Trump’s coveted elections bill, known as the “SAVE America Act.”

“If they never get the SAVE America Act done, you have the right to declare a national security emergency for elections,” Root said. He added that “if you declare a national security emergency as the president of the United States, they can’t challenge it. It can only be overturned by a two-thirds vote by both houses of Congress. So if you do this in the next month, we will get photo ID, proof of citizenship (for voter registration) and a limit to mail-in ballots.”

It’s at this point that Trump cut Root off and coyly suggested such an option was indeed in play.

“Let me just say that stranger things have happened, OK?” Trump said. “I’ll leave it at that.”

Despite Root’s comments, it’s far from clear such a gambit would even work. And CNN has asked the White House for more detail on what the president meant.

Trump often responds to hypotheticals by declining to rule them out — no matter how extreme the proposal might be. So it’s possible to read too much into this.

But as CNN’s Jake Tapper has noted, there are plenty of signals that Trump at least aspires to try to exert more control over elections. And these methods often appear transparently geared toward helping Republicans.
